exclusion_technique: Assign an existing IAM role to a controlled Identity Center user through Account Access Manager
review_evidence: Current exclusion notes missing proof that the source controls the Identity Center subject; inspect exact entitlement subject and effective permissions.

AWS confirms management/delegated-admin principals can change a member account root email after StartPrimaryEmailUpdate, AcceptPrimaryEmailUpdate and the new-email OTP. Email control alone does not establish root sign-in: root MFA and Organizations central root credential recovery can block it. Need exact member-account recovery and MFA evidence plus organization/delegation scope before an account-admin edge; AWS AcceptPrimaryEmailUpdate, Update root user email, and Root MFA docs.
Old YAML omitted the source IAM action/resource and target credential subject; inspect page for a collectable exact chain.

GetApp/ListApps and branch/job reads can disclose deployment variables or build logs, but the CSPM stores only secret indicators, not credential values. The page supplies no verified AWS credential subject, usability or added IAM action. Keep this as data disclosure until exact credential evidence exists; AWS Amplify GetApp/GetBranch/GetJob APIs.

exclusion_technique: Change an Amplify app build specification and start a build
review_evidence: ListApps retains exact iamServiceRoleArn, but the CSPM does not collect app branches, repository/RELEASE readiness, effective buildspec precedence or a controlled executable build input. Add exact branch and job-scope IAM joins and a verified code-delivery witness before restoring UpdateApp plus StartJob to the existing build role; AWS UpdateApp and StartJob APIs.

exclusion_technique: Change an Amplify branch's build environment variables and start a build
review_evidence: HackTricks records a live branch environment-hook proof, but current CSPM does not collect exact branch ARN, branch-to-app role join or evidence that a writable hook exists and the build starts its interpreter. UpdateBranch buildSpec may be stored without running. Collect the join and execution witness before restoring; AWS UpdateBranch/StartJob APIs and HackTricks live proof.

exclusion_technique: Recover a live Amplify Studio administrator login
review_evidence: GetToken can recover the challenge for a known live Amplify Studio session; it does not itself issue IAM credentials. A Studio admin may later change backend resources that run with an AWS role, so exclude a principal edge until the exact session, post-login operation and role execution path are proven.

exclusion_technique: Update an existing App Runner service that has an instance role
review_evidence: DescribeService yields exact InstanceRoleArn and image-source type; a RUNNING service, matching role, same-account/Region ARN and service-scoped UpdateService grant are required. Positive and wrong-role, wrong-Region, inactive, code-source and missing-permission negatives in tests/test_peaso_privesc_apprunner_existing_role.py; AWS UpdateService and DescribeService APIs.

exclusion_technique: Connect to an existing app block builder that has an IAM role
review_evidence: Exact recorded RUNNING builder ARN and IamRoleArn joined to resource-scoped streaming permission; positive and negative cases in tests/test_peaso_privesc_appstream_existing_builders.py; AWS AppStream API and Service Authorization Reference.

exclusion_technique: Connect to an existing image builder that has an IAM role
review_evidence: Exact recorded RUNNING builder ARN and IamRoleArn joined to resource-scoped streaming permission; positive and negative cases in tests/test_peaso_privesc_appstream_existing_builders.py; AWS AppStream API and Service Authorization Reference.

exclusion_technique: Change the launch definition of an application used by an Elastic fleet
review_evidence: AWS UpdateApplication changes LaunchPath/LaunchParameters on one application ARN. DescribeApplicationFleetAssociations joins that exact application to a fleet; DescribeFleets supplies FleetType, State and IamRoleArn. CSPM collects fleets but neither applications nor application-fleet associations, and evaluator has no exact update-to-role join. A later entitled-user launch or authorized streaming URL remains conditional. Keep excluded until collector and scoped IAM join distinguish associated Elastic fleets with a role; AWS UpdateApplication, DescribeApplicationFleetAssociations, Fleet and Applications docs.

exclusion_technique: Attach a passed role to an IAM-signed HTTP data source and call it through a resolver
review_evidence: The self-contained new-API variant is restored as aws-appsync-passrole-new-api-sigv4 with all five global AppSync setup actions, exact role PassRole and AppSync trust. The existing-API variant still needs a collected callable field and authorization path; AWS AppSync API and Service Authorization Reference.

An existing HTTP data source with AWS_IAM signing and a recorded serviceRoleArn could proxy AWS calls if the source can change and invoke a reachable resolver. CSPM currently collects only API summaries, not data sources, field bindings or usable invocation authorization. Fixed DynamoDB/OpenSearch/RDS backends do not imply general role authority; AWS AppSync resolver and HTTP data-source docs.

AWS Region Switch does not return the passed plan role or its general IAM authority; the retired full-role edge is excluded_verified. A distinct SSMSendCommand execution block can call SendCommand through the plan role and may lead to a selected managed node’s instance role when a Command document, parameters, online node, role permission and execution path are joined. That distinct path remains an unresolved page-level candidate; it has no active YAML entry or separate retired-technique row. AWS Region Switch SSM execution-block and role-policy guides.

exclusion_technique: Mint a presigned URL for a running Athena Spark notebook
review_evidence: Restored with complete ListSessions/GetSession evidence for the exact session role, engine, state and workgroup; source IAM grant is checked on the exact workgroup. Notebook URL additionally requires NotebookVersion. Missing or denied detail remains unknown; tests/test_peaso_privesc_athena_sessions.py; AWS GetSession, SessionStatus, Spark API support and Athena Service Authorization Reference.

exclusion_technique: Submit a calculation to an existing Athena Spark session
review_evidence: Restored with complete ListSessions/GetSession evidence for the exact session role, engine, state and workgroup; source IAM grant is checked on the exact workgroup. Notebook URL additionally requires NotebookVersion. Missing or denied detail remains unknown; tests/test_peaso_privesc_athena_sessions.py; AWS GetSession, SessionStatus, Spark API support and Athena Service Authorization Reference.

exclusion_technique: Replace the cells of an Athena Spark notebook that is executed later
review_evidence: GetWorkGroup retains Configuration.ExecutionRole, but no notebook inventory or later execution linkage is collected. UpdateNotebook alone changes stored cells; it does not prove code ran under the role. Need exact notebook-to-workgroup attachment and execution trigger before restoring.

CreateAssociation can target an online hybrid managed node with an AWS shell document, but the current active evaluator covers EC2 instance-profile nodes only. A definite hybrid role edge needs that node's recorded IamRole, platform, exact association and document permissions, command parameters and node processing; DescribeInstanceInformation supplies IamRole and PingStatus. AWS SSM InstanceInformation and CreateAssociation docs.

AWS CreateScheduledQuery accepts SQL, a fixed Timestream target, an SNS notification and an S3 error-report destination under a passed execution role. Those are bounded data/workflow effects; the caller receives the scheduled-query ARN, not role credentials or an arbitrary AWS action. The HackTricks Cloud privesc page already classifies this as post-exploitation. No exact principal-to-principal edge. AWS CreateScheduledQuery API, scheduled-query concepts and service authorization reference.

The management-account caller may enable Organizations IAM trusted access and root sessions, then call AssumeRoot for a member account if it also has sts:AssumeRoot. The returned credential is still restricted to one mandatory root task policy. Candidate requires exact management scope, existing trusted-access/feature state, all effective grants, member target and bounded task authority; no full root-admin edge (AWS AssumeRoot API and centralized root access guide).

UpdateInstance can enable permission sets, but that setting creates no access alone. A route needs UpdateInstance when disabled, a usable permission set or rights to create and attach one, CreateAccountAssignment to an exact controlled Identity Center user/group in a member account, successful provisioning and working portal login. Candidate because the current collector records instance/user/set metadata but not source control of the directory identity or a full resulting role join (AWS UpdateInstance and CreateAccountAssignment APIs).

This TestState HTTP Task variant discloses a third-party EventBridge Connection credential, not IAM permissions of a different AWS principal. Its source actions states:TestState and iam:PassRole and target role are already modeled by active aws-stepfunctions-teststate-passrole for the AWS principal-to-principal route. The additional HTTP Task requirements and external secret belong to credential exposure analysis, not a second AWS role edge. Keep excluded from principal graph; HackTricks source and AWS Step Functions HTTP Task docs.

AWS ListStreamUrls can return an active bearer URL and GetStreamUrl can return its RoleArn, but the URL starts the already configured interactive application. It does not give the browser caller IAM role credentials or a general command channel; application behavior and any credential exposure are separate facts. An exact role ARN alongside a URL is insufficient for principal-to-principal escalation. Keep the URL disclosure as a post-exploitation risk, not an executable IAM path; AWS ListStreamUrls and GetStreamUrl APIs.

The recovered IVS stream key, SRT passphrase or ingest credential authorizes media publishing or playback for a channel/stage. AWS GetStreamKey returns a stream-key value and its channel ARN, not STS or IAM credentials. Retain as media-plane capability, not an aws_role transition (AWS GetStreamKey API and HackTricks IVS post-exploitation page).

The recovered IVS stream key, SRT passphrase or ingest credential authorizes media publishing or playback for a channel/stage. AWS GetStreamKey returns a stream-key value and its channel ARN, not STS or IAM credentials. Retain as media-plane capability, not an aws_role transition (AWS GetStreamKey API and HackTricks IVS post-exploitation page).

The recovered IVS stream key, SRT passphrase or ingest credential authorizes media publishing or playback for a channel/stage. AWS GetStreamKey returns a stream-key value and its channel ARN, not STS or IAM credentials. Retain as media-plane capability, not an aws_role transition (AWS GetStreamKey API and HackTricks IVS post-exploitation page).

AWS JIT access can authorize a temporary Session Manager connection only after an applicable auto-approval or all manual approvals; a deny policy wins. Hybrid nodes use an SSM service role, but the role attached to the exact managed node and its approval decision are not in the CSPM join. Shell access may expose node credentials, but the role gain must not be inferred from StartAccessRequest/GetAccessToken alone. Keep this hybrid-specific route excluded until managed-node/activation-role and approval joins are collected; AWS JIT and hybrid service-role docs.

Lake Formation can assume the custom role used to register an S3 location and vend credentials scoped to that location through an integrated engine. RegisterResource with privileged access gives the caller DATA_LOCATION_ACCESS, but that grant alone does not permit reading bytes. Need exact unregistered location, selected passable role and its S3/KMS authority, caller table and query permissions, and a runnable engine before claiming added role-backed data access. A vended session remains scoped to the registered prefix, not arbitrary role authority; AWS registration and underlying data access docs.

AWS WorkDocs UpdateUser can set Type=ADMIN for one WorkDocs user ID; this is site administration, not an IAM role or AWS-wide permission. The retired entry lacks both a source-controlled login link and an exact IAM action/resource requirement; do not restore it as a principal edge. AWS WorkDocs UpdateUser CLI docs.

UpdateConnector can redirect an SFTP connector while retaining its stored partner credential, but that credential authenticates to an external SFTP server, not another AWS IAM principal. A later connection is also needed before disclosure. Keep this conditional partner-data route outside the AWS principal graph; AWS UpdateConnector API and Transfer Family page.

AWS CreateDataRetentionBotChallenge returns a new password to authenticate a Wickr data-retention bot to one Wickr network. It can expose message content if the bot is operated, but the bot is not an IAM role and the API grants no AWS principal rights. Retain as Wickr application takeover (AWS CreateDataRetentionBotChallenge API).

AWS ResumeSession returns StreamUrl and TokenValue for a disconnected session and is authorized on the exact session ARN, not the node ARN. A shell session could expose the node role, but a port-forward session does not itself provide shell access. CSPM collects neither DescribeSessions state/document/target nor the hybrid node role join, and cannot establish that the source may resume that exact session or use its stream. Restore only after those joins and session-owner restrictions are checked; AWS ResumeSession and SSM service authorization docs.

CreateAccessPolicy grants a chosen IAM or Identity Center identity permission on a SiteWise Monitor portal or project; it does not change IAM policy or let the caller assume that identity. A self-grant is bounded to Monitor content and requires an account already enrolled for that feature. The previous source anchor pointed to a post-exploitation page that no longer contained this route; corrected to the actual privesc page. AWS CreateAccessPolicy API.

AWS StartAssociationsOnce accepts only existing association IDs and runs the stored document on its stored targets once. The call supplies no replacement document, command, target, output destination or role. Running fixed code under a node role does not itself grant the caller that role. A separately writable document/parameter or output path must be modeled as its own joined route. Excluded from principal-to-principal YAML; AWS StartAssociationsOnce API.

AWS StartCanary takes only the canary name and runs its stored code/schedule; it accepts no attacker-selected command, input, role or output destination. GetCanary exposes ExecutionRoleArn, but that attachment alone does not give the caller the role permissions or a controllable side effect. Treat a separate writable code/input or result-access path as a different technique. Excluded from principal-to-principal YAML; AWS StartCanary and Canary APIs.

AWS ExecuteScheduledQuery accepts only an existing scheduled-query ARN and invocation time, returns an empty success body, and runs its stored SQL asynchronously. It cannot replace the stored role, SQL, target or notification in that call. This is a bounded existing workflow, not another principal. AWS ExecuteScheduledQuery API and scheduled-query concepts.

AWS AppConfig Data StartConfigurationSession returns a token for a selected application, environment and profile; GetLatestConfiguration returns its deployed configuration bytes. Those bytes may contain sensitive values, but neither call assumes an IAM role or proves a usable AWS credential and subject. The HackTricks Cloud page covers configuration disclosure in post-exploitation. Verified exclusion from principal-to-principal YAML; AWS AppConfig Data APIs.

GetGraphqlApiEnvironmentVariables and GetIntrospectionSchema disclose application values and schema; the page does not establish a usable IAM credential subject or another AWS principal. Keep as data exposure, not a privilege edge; HackTricks AppSync post-exploitation page and AWS AppSync API.

GetQueryExecution returns the SQL text and metadata for a known query execution. SQL literals may disclose data, but this API does not issue AWS credentials, assume a role or identify a newly usable principal. The HackTricks Cloud page treats it as query-history disclosure. Verified exclusion from principal-to-principal YAML; AWS GetQueryExecution and QueryExecution APIs.

GetQueryResults returns rows for a known completed execution only when the caller can also read its S3 result object; a direct S3 read can retrieve the same file. Those rows may be sensitive, but the permission does not itself provide another IAM principal or session. A credential-bearing row would require separate observed content and target identity. Verified exclusion from principal-to-principal YAML; AWS GetQueryResults API and HackTricks Cloud query-disclosure page.

exclusion_technique: Submit a job using an existing job definition with a job role
review_evidence: Restored using a projected ACTIVE EC2 job definition and exact versioned ARN, recorded jobRoleArn, valid enabled EC2 queue and SubmitJob permission on both resources. Wrong revision, queue, state, platform and grant negatives pass; tests/test_peaso_privesc_batch_existing_definition.py; AWS SubmitJob and IAM restrict-job-submission docs.

exclusion_technique: Run code in an existing AgentCore Code Interpreter with an execution role
review_evidence: AWS GetCodeInterpreter returns exact codeInterpreterArn, executionRoleArn and status. A READY custom interpreter plus StartCodeInterpreterSession and InvokeCodeInterpreter on its exact ARN can establish role reach. CSPM does not collect List/GetCodeInterpreters or join this role to the source action; add safe inventory and tests before restoring. AWS GetCodeInterpreter and InvokeCodeInterpreter APIs.

exclusion_technique: Run shell commands in an existing AgentCore agent runtime
review_evidence: InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand executes supplied shell commands only in an active session of an exact runtime ARN. GetHarness returns executionRoleArn and environment.agentCoreRuntimeEnvironment.agentRuntimeArn; GetAgentRuntime returns roleArn. Authorization also covers the selected runtime endpoint and both resource policies. CSPM has no exact runtime/role/endpoint/policy/session join, so permission on an unrelated runtime cannot justify restoring this route. AWS GetHarness, InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand and resource-policy docs.

exclusion_technique: Invoke an existing AgentCore harness with its shell tool to run commands as its execution role
review_evidence: Indirect prompt injection requires attacker-controlled content to reach an existing harness, shell to be allowed, and the model to choose the shell tool. GetHarness can identify role and allowedTools, but these facts do not prove model behavior or an exact controllable input path; do not report a definite principal transition from InvokeHarness alone. AWS Harness security and GetHarness docs.

billing:UpdateIAMAccessPreference changes the account Allow IAM Access preference but neither supplies a target identity nor creates an IAM grant. Another principal may gain access only through billing permissions already attached to it; the source does not obtain that principal credentials or role. If the source itself has dormant billing grants this is its own bounded permission activation, not principal-to-principal escalation. Keep excluded from the AWS principal graph; AWS Billing authorization and account access docs.

AWS CreateSlackChannelConfiguration requires an authorized Slack workspace and accepts IamRoleArn, guardrails, and UserAuthorizationRequired; AWS service authorization lists iam:PassRole. A source-to-role edge also requires proof that this AWS caller controls a member of the exact channel, channel-role use is allowed by account user-role policy, and a usable chat command grants new authority. AWS explicitly blocks iam:*, sts:*, kms:*, secretsmanager:*, and s3:GetObject commands in chat. No linked AWS-caller-to-chat-identity or channel membership evidence exists in CSPM; candidate remains unresolved. AWS CreateSlackChannelConfiguration API, Understanding permissions, and service authorization reference.

GetAttendee/ListAttendees can return a JoinToken for an exact Chime meeting attendee. The token permits meeting participation until deletion or expiry, but it is not an IAM or STS credential and grants no AWS role actions. Retain as bounded meeting access (AWS GetAttendee API and Chime attendee guide).

GetMediaPipeline can disclose an RTMP(S) destination URL containing a downstream stream key. That key lets a publisher affect the media destination, not assume a Chime service role or AWS principal. Retain as media credential disclosure (HackTricks Chime SDK enumeration page).

exclusion_technique: Replace a mutable nested-stack template object in S3
review_evidence: A writable S3 object may hold the TemplateURL of a nested stack and later run under its stored CloudFormation service role. The exact parent-template URL and current object version, source PutObject authorization, a later change that actually updates that child, and a role-permitted privilege-changing resource are not joined. AWS says unchanged nested stacks are not updated merely because the root updates. Keep as a candidate until those facts support a specific role edge.

exclusion_technique: Overwrite a Parameter Store value that a stack resolves as a template parameter
review_evidence: A CloudFormation-supplied SSM parameter type uses the latest value of the same Parameter Store key on a later stack update, even with UsePreviousValue. The current collector does not join an exact writable parameter key to a stack template property such as ManagedPolicyArns, the resulting target identity, and the stored stack role. An unversioned dynamic reference is not equivalent for every update. Keep as a candidate until the exact consumer and resulting privilege change are established.

UpdateStackSet can update existing stack instances, but the recorded StackSet inventory has only summary and instance rows, not its AdministrationRoleARN or ExecutionRoleName. The existing PassRole StackSet route covers a selected administration role; this separate route would need an exact SELF_MANAGED StackSet, matching instance account and region, stored role association, authorized UpdateStackSet scope, and a role-permitted template effect. Keep candidate pending DescribeStackSet and execution-role join.

AWS says GetSpaceCredentialsForOrganization returns one-hour credentials scoped to an existing member-account space, and the response contains keys but no IAM principal ARN (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cloudwatch-omni/latest/APIReference/API_GetSpaceCredentialsForOrganization.html). The GetSpace dataAccessRoleArn is a permission ceiling, while member grants further limit use (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/omni-security-best-practices-for-cloudwatch-omni.html). Static inventory cannot prove those credentials represent the full named IAM role or identify a second principal, so the old aws_role edge was an overclaim; retain the excluded credential route.

exclusion_technique: Publish a newer compatible version of a trusted CodeArtifact package consumed by a privileged workload
review_evidence: Old route lacks an exact package-to-consumer-to-role join; inspect CodeArtifact consumer inventory and package version selection.

exclusion_technique: Overwrite a Parameter Store value consumed as a CodeBuild environment variable
review_evidence: CodeBuild resolves a PARAMETER_STORE environment reference when a build starts. The CSPM project projection discards environment variable values, including the referenced parameter name, and does not inspect the buildspec use of that variable. PutParameter on a guessed key cannot prove code execution as the project serviceRole; the value might only affect data or fail the build. Keep candidate pending exact key-to-project, buildspec-consumer and execution-path joins.

exclusion_technique: Overwrite a Secrets Manager value consumed as a CodeBuild environment variable
review_evidence: CodeBuild resolves a SECRETS_MANAGER environment reference when a build starts. The CSPM project projection discards environment variable values, including the referenced secret ID, and does not inspect the buildspec use of that variable. PutSecretValue on a guessed secret cannot prove code execution as the project serviceRole; the value might only affect data or fail the build. Keep candidate pending exact secret-to-project, buildspec-consumer and execution-path joins.

AWS BatchGetProjects can return PLAINTEXT environment values, including an accidentally stored AWS access-key pair. CSPM deliberately redacts values and retains only secret categories, so it cannot currently prove that both parts form a usable credential or bind the access key ID to a different IAM principal. A CodeBuild project with generic secret indicators is insufficient for a role edge. Keep excluded pending a privacy-preserving exact credential-owner and source BatchGetProjects authorization join; AWS CodeBuild environment variable docs.

exclusion_technique: Replace the S3 source object of a CodeBuild project
review_evidence: An S3-sourced CodeBuild project may execute attacker-controlled source or buildspec bytes as its serviceRole after its configured object is replaced. The CSPM project projection redacts the exact source location and preserves no bucket/key-to-project join; it also lacks a witness that the buildspec executes changed bytes and that a build can start. A fixed separate buildspec can limit what a ZIP replacement changes. Keep candidate pending exact source object, PutObject scope, execution and role joins.

exclusion_technique: Push a CodeCommit source revision executed by a CodeBuild project
review_evidence: CodeCommit GitPush can alter a buildspec or script consumed by a CodeBuild project and run under its serviceRole, but the current codecommit_build_links view marks BuildSpecUsesInput and ExecutionPathAvailable unknown. Exact branch-aware GitPush, source revision, project source/buildspec and trigger need to be joined. A pipeline link alone does not prove that the changed content executes. Keep excluded until those preconditions are verifiable; AWS CodeBuild buildspec and CodeCommit branch docs. The recorded link now includes same-stage source/build actions only when source runOrder precedes build runOrder; isolated ordering cases passed.

exclusion_technique: Push to a CodeCommit repository branch used as a pipeline source
review_evidence: AWS CodeCommit source action names an exact RepositoryName and BranchName, and CodePipeline may start by polling or EventBridge. CSPM has projected pipeline source metadata but its prepared codecommit_build_links view leaves BranchWritable, ExecutionPathAvailable and VerifiedPreconditions unset. IAM GitPush must be checked with codecommit:References for that branch, followed by the exact source artifact and executing downstream role. Keep excluded until that join proves a role-running consumer; AWS CodeCommit source and branch policy docs. The recorded link now includes same-stage source/build actions only when source runOrder precedes build runOrder; isolated ordering cases passed.

exclusion_technique: Push to a CodeCommit branch used as the source of a CloudFormation-deploying pipeline
review_evidence: A CodeCommit branch can feed a CloudFormation deploy stage, but the current collector projection retains CodeCommit source and CodeBuild actions only; it drops CloudFormation action configuration and its stack/template role join. A GitPush grant on the repository must cover the configured branch, and the pushed template must be the exact deploy input before the CloudFormation role can be the target. Keep excluded pending downstream action and artifact/role collection; AWS CodeCommit source action docs.

exclusion_technique: Point a CloudFormation Git sync configuration at a controlled branch with a passed sync role
review_evidence: CreateSyncConfiguration or UpdateSyncConfiguration can name a Git-sync role and a repository link, branch and deployment file. The source must also control that exact external Git content and the link must be usable; IAM PassRole plus PassRepository does not prove either condition. CSPM has no repository-link, sync-config or external branch-write join. Candidate pending an exact source-control and role/template-effect witness.

UpdateConnectionInstallation can bind an AWS connection to a third-party installation through an authorization handshake, but the caller must complete that provider flow. It is not a standalone write API and does not itself confer another AWS principal. A principal edge requires a downstream Git-sync or pipeline consumer, exact repository/branch control and its execution role; CSPM collects none of that chain. Candidate pending those joins.

exclusion_technique: Redirect a repository link consumed by CloudFormation Git sync to a controlled connection
review_evidence: UpdateRepositoryLink changes the connection or KMS key of an existing repository link, not its repository owner or name. An AWS role path needs a usable same-provider replacement connection that reaches that same repository, attacker control of a monitored branch/file, an existing Git-sync configuration consuming the link, and its target role. None follows from UpdateRepositoryLink permission alone; candidate pending those exact joins. AWS UpdateRepositoryLink API.

exclusion_technique: Deploy a controlled revision to an existing EC2/on-premises deployment group
review_evidence: CreateDeployment can deliver a controlled revision whose lifecycle hooks run on EC2 or on-premises hosts. The collector records deployment-group targeting rules but not an exact currently reachable instance, its instance profile, a valid attacker-controlled revision, or a working agent. Host root is not by itself another IAM principal. Candidate pending revision, target-host/profile and executable-hook joins; AWS CodeDeploy service authorization and AppSpec docs.

AWS GetJobDetails returns STS artifact credentials for an existing custom-action job when artifacts require them; it takes a known job UUID. Need job existence, credential subject and effective added AWS permissions, not only codepipeline:GetJobDetails. AWS GetJobDetails and AWSSessionCredentials API docs.

AWS PollForJobs returns STS artifact credentials for a matching pending Custom action when artifacts require them; AWS and ThirdParty owners are rejected. Need exact action tuple, pending job, credential subject and effective added AWS permissions, not only codepipeline:PollForJobs. AWS PollForJobs and AWSSessionCredentials API docs.

exclusion_technique: Replace the S3 source object of a pipeline
review_evidence: An S3 source action reads an exact bucket/key and passes a source artifact downstream; a new object can trigger the pipeline. The collector does not join source key, source version, downstream executable use of the artifact, trigger, and target build role. S3 PutObject on the key alone cannot prove role execution; candidate pending exact source-to-consumer and role joins. AWS S3 source action docs.

exclusion_technique: Replace the S3 source object of a pipeline that deploys through CloudFormation
review_evidence: A pipeline S3 source may feed a CloudFormation deploy action, but source ZIP replacement alone does not show that the deploy action consumes a changed template or which CloudFormation role applies it. Need exact source artifact mapping, deploy action template path, approved capabilities, execution trigger and target role permission effect. Keep candidate pending those joins; AWS S3 source and CloudFormation action docs.

exclusion_technique: Add a user-pool user the source controls to a group with an IAM role
review_evidence: AWS confirms AdminAddUserToGroup changes cognito:groups and possibly cognito:preferred_role claims. The collector records group RoleArn and identity-pool provider mapping, but does not record a source-controlled user, that user’s sign-in token, group precedence, or the exact identity-pool role selected. Keep as a principal pivot candidate until those joins are collected; AWS AdminAddUserToGroup and Adding groups to a user pool docs.

AWS confirms AdminConfirmSignUp can confirm a registered user without the normal confirmation code. A role edge requires a source-controlled self-registered user, an app client that accepts its sign-in, completed authentication and exact identity-pool role selection. The collector has pool/client configuration but no per-user registration or token ownership. AWS Signing up and confirming user accounts and Cognito role-based access docs.

exclusion_technique: Create a user in a user pool
review_evidence: AWS confirms AdminCreateUser normally creates a FORCE_CHANGE_PASSWORD user; completing the challenge or another configured passwordless flow is needed before the user receives an ID token. The collector has pool/client settings but no created-user credential or completed sign-in, and rule-mapped roles cannot be inferred from the operation alone. Candidate for a combined creation/authentication/default-role route; AWS Creating user accounts as administrator and Cognito role-based access docs.

exclusion_technique: Link a federated identity the source controls to an existing user-pool user
review_evidence: AWS confirms AdminLinkProviderForUser attaches an external IdP subject to an existing local user profile, which then supplies that profile’s access settings at sign-in. A principal edge needs the source-controlled external subject and claim, accepted app client, existing destination user and exact resulting role. None is linked by the current collector; AWS AdminLinkProviderForUser and Linking federated users docs.

exclusion_technique: Set the password of an existing user-pool user
review_evidence: AWS confirms AdminSetUserPassword with Permanent=true can permit immediate password sign-in, including for a previously federated profile. The collector does not identify the selected user, the source’s control of its credential, MFA/app-client acceptance or that user’s exact group/rule-mapped IAM role. Keep candidate; AWS AdminSetUserPassword and Cognito role-based access docs.

exclusion_technique: Change a user-pool user's attributes to match an identity-pool role-mapping rule
review_evidence: Changing a user-pool attribute can select an identity-pool rule role only if the source controls that user and can produce an accepted ID token whose claim satisfies the specific rule. The collector records RoleMappings and pool/client metadata but not controlled user attributes or token claims. Candidate until source subject, claim and exact rule role are joined; AWS Cognito role-based access docs.

exclusion_technique: Add or change a federated identity provider of a user pool
review_evidence: Create/UpdateIdentityProvider can change the upstream IdP used by a user pool, but the source must control a sign-in subject at that IdP and an app client must accept the provider. The collector records provider names/types and client settings, not proof of external IdP subject control or the resulting token-to-role mapping. Candidate, not a definite IAM-role edge; AWS Cognito user-pool federation and role-based access docs.

exclusion_technique: Create or update a user-pool group with a passed role
review_evidence: AWS group documentation confirms a group RoleArn can enter cognito:roles and preferred_role claims, but CreateGroup/UpdateGroup plus PassRole does not place a source-controlled user in the group. Group precedence, app-client sign-in, identity-pool role selection and target trust must be joined. The collector records groups and role ARNs but not controlled membership/token; candidate pending exact chain. AWS Adding groups to a user pool and Cognito role-based access docs.

DescribeIdentityProvider can return an upstream OAuth client secret, but a client secret alone does not authenticate as an upstream user or establish an AWS principal. A definite role edge would require a usable upstream identity, an app client that accepts it, and an exact token-to-role mapping. The current collector has no such join. AWS DescribeIdentityProvider API reference.

exclusion_technique: Mint a developer-authenticated identity token for an identity pool
review_evidence: The developer-token API authorizes a specific identity-pool ARN. The collector records DeveloperProviderName and the exact authenticated role; the CSPM joins only that role and checks the pool audience and authenticated Cognito web-identity trust. Different-pool permission, missing provider, absent authenticated role, incompatible trust, explicit deny and incomplete collection do not yield a concrete edge. Evaluator and archive-binding tests cover the route; AWS GetOpenIdTokenForDeveloperIdentity, GetCredentialsForIdentity and GetIdentityPoolRoles docs.

exclusion_technique: Set the roles of an identity pool the source can obtain credentials from
review_evidence: The exact developer-token subset is active as aws-cognito-setidentitypoolroles-developer-token. If AllowUnauthenticatedIdentities is enabled, the source may also assign a trusted guest role and obtain guest credentials without signing in. Cognito applies a scope-down policy to enhanced-flow guest credentials, so treating them as full target-role authority is unsound. Model guest-session effective permissions before promoting this separate subset. User-pool token routes still need a controlled subject and exact role selection. AWS SetIdentityPoolRoles and Cognito IAM roles guides.

exclusion_technique: Remap identity-pool principal tags to attributes the source controls
review_evidence: SetPrincipalTagAttributeMap changes which identity-provider claim becomes a session principal tag. The target is authority within an existing role through aws:PrincipalTag conditions, not the whole role. A definite edge needs a source-controlled token claim, exact tag mapping, trust allowing sts:TagSession and a concrete policy condition whose result changes. Those facts are not joined by the collector. AWS Cognito attributes-for-access-control guide.

exclusion_technique: Add a provider the source controls to an identity pool
review_evidence: UpdateIdentityPool can add a provider or enable guests. The exact principal-to-role guest Basic-flow subset is now active as aws-cognito-updateidentitypool-enable-guest-classic-role: source update on one collected pool, no role mappings, guest token and matching role trust. The developer-token Basic-flow subset is also active. Other provider-token paths still require a source-controlled accepted token and exact selected role. Enhanced-flow guest credentials alone are session scoped and do not grant the full role. AWS UpdateIdentityPool, Cognito authentication-flow and IAM roles docs.

exclusion_technique: Enable the basic (classic) authentication flow on an identity pool
review_evidence: Two exact subsets are implemented. The developer route needs same-pool UpdateIdentityPool and GetOpenIdTokenForDeveloperIdentity, plus matching authenticated role trust. The guest route needs same-pool UpdateIdentityPool, complete empty RoleMappings and matching unauthenticated role trust; public GetId/GetOpenIdToken then supplies the token. Other user-pool/provider routes still need proof of a usable controlled token and exact role selection. AWS UpdateIdentityPool, Cognito authentication-flow and IAM roles docs.

The documented read can expose a social or OIDC provider client secret, but this credential identifies an application at the upstream provider, not an AWS role or a user. A principal pivot requires a separately proved upstream user login, accepted Cognito app client, and exact target role. The collector does not establish that chain. AWS DescribeIdentityProvider API reference.

exclusion_technique: Import users with known passwords via a user import job
review_evidence: AWS now supports importing password hashes, which can create CONFIRMED users able to sign in immediately; passwordless import can also do so. This overturns the old blanket RESET_REQUIRED reason, but a principal edge still needs CreateUserImportJob and StartUserImportJob access, a passable logs role, an accepted app-client sign-in and exact identity-pool role selection. The current collector does not join these facts. AWS Importing users into user pools from a CSV file guide.

GetContactAttributes returns an arbitrary contact attribute string map, not AWS credentials or an IAM subject (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/APIReference/API_GetContactAttributes.html). A customer might place a key in a contact field or attachment, but the exact content, validity, subject, and additional authority are not established by contact metadata or the API grant. That is a possible contact-data exposure, not a verified principal-to-principal edge.

Connect monitoring exposes live conversation content, not a named AWS principal or credentials by itself (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/adminguide/monitor-conversations-howto.html). A customer would have to disclose a usable AWS secret in a specific conversation, and its subject and additional authority would have to be verified. IAM permission to monitor cannot establish any of those facts; retain outside the exact principal graph.

CreateParticipant returns a bearer for an ongoing Connect chat or WebRTC contact. AWS says it is used with the Connect Participant API, not as an AWS SigV4 or STS credential; the token grants bounded contact participation, not another AWS IAM principal. Keep this application credential outside the IAM principal graph.

DescribeContactFlow returns flow Content JSON (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/APIReference/API_DescribeContactFlow.html). A referenced Lambda, integration ARN, or arbitrary string in that JSON is not its IAM role credentials. A hard-coded AWS key would require actual content analysis, credential subject validation, and added-authority comparison; flow-read authorization alone proves no principal edge.

A custom chat message processor may receive eligible message content, but processor configuration is neither a credential nor evidence that a customer sent a usable AWS key. The route requires an active attached processor, the specific message, validated IAM credential subject, and added authority. Those are absent from static Connect inventory, so the old generic verified-authority edge was unsupported; this remains a conversation-data route.

exclusion_technique: Impersonate a SAML Connect user by choosing the role-session name
review_evidence: Choosing RoleSessionName for a permitted Connect federation role can map the session to another Connect user and return Connect access/refresh tokens. Those tokens administer the Connect application only; they do not create another AWS IAM session. The STS assumption of the federation role is a separate IAM trust route already represented by role-assumption checks.

exclusion_technique: Grant Connect Admin through security-profile assignment or mutation
review_evidence: UpdateUserSecurityProfiles or UpdateSecurityProfile can grant a controlled Connect user application administration, but Connect security profiles are a separate application authorization layer. They do not grant IAM actions or another AWS principal credentials; report this as Connect privilege exposure, not an IAM principal edge.

StartContactStreaming enables an SNS endpoint for an exact chat and returns only a StreamingId (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/APIReference/API_StartContactStreaming.html); AWS documents SNS delivery of message payloads (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/adminguide/chat-message-streaming.html). A streaming configuration does not prove that a message contains a usable AWS credential, identify its principal, or establish additional IAM permissions. The route is contact-data exposure until those facts are observed.

exclusion_technique: Take over a Connect-managed user by changing its email
review_evidence: UpdateUserIdentityInfo may replace a Connect-managed user email and enable a password reset, as AWS warns. The result is takeover of a Connect application user and its security-profile permissions, not the user's AWS IAM identity or role credentials. Keep this service-level issue outside the IAM principal graph.

exclusion_technique: Update an Account Factory provisioned account to grant AWSAdministratorAccess to a controlled Identity Center user
review_evidence: AWS Account Factory can update a provisioned account and create a new Identity Center user for a new email, but effective access needs source control of that mailbox/user, exact resulting assignment and target member account. Provisioning also needs management-account permissions, an enabled OU baseline and async success. AWS Account Factory and provisioning permissions docs.

DisableControl changes an OU guardrail asynchronously, but no second principal follows from the call alone. Keep as a candidate for an exact before/after join between the disabled control, account/OU scope, a previously denied source action and a resulting target-role route; generic control changes stay out of the YAML.

AWS CreateLocationS3 binds BucketAccessRoleArn to an S3 transfer location. CreateTask and StartTaskExecution copy selected data through the role but do not return its credentials or general IAM authority. The original aws_role target is an overclaim; S3 disclosure/tampering remains a separate data finding. AWS CreateLocationS3 API.

AWS UpdateLocationS3 can replace the role or prefix on one existing S3 location; the bucket and task location pair remain fixed. Starting the task can copy selected S3 objects, not provide the role identity or broad permissions. The old aws_role target is unsupported. AWS UpdateLocationS3 API.

AWS CreateProjectMembership can add a controlled IAM/SSO profile as project member only when the caller has DataZone project-owner/domain authorization and the domain-unit membership policy allows that member. A role edge needs that same profile to hold datazone:GetEnvironmentCredentials, a live environment in that project, its exact associated IAM role, and an effective issued session with additional permissions. The API returns STS credentials but a session policy can remove sts:AssumeRole, so do not equate it with all role authority. Current CSPM does not collect or join project ownership, profile identity, membership policy, environment-to-role binding or session restrictions; retain as a candidate, never infer from CreateProjectMembership alone. AWS CreateProjectMembership, GetEnvironmentCredentials and Add members to a project docs.

AWS GetEnvironmentCredentials returns temporary AWS credentials for an exact environment; GetEnvironment includes projectId and provisioned role references, while ListProjectMemberships plus GetUserProfile can join a caller to that project. The page observes a session policy excluding sts:AssumeRole, so targeting the full IAM role would overstate access. CSPM currently collects none of those DataZone facts; implement a bounded role-session route only after exact role, membership, environment state and session-policy semantics are joined. AWS DataZone APIs.

AssociateEnvironmentRole names the exact role, and project members can later call GetEnvironmentCredentials. A route needs exact domain/environment/project membership, IAM PassRole and service trust, as well as a model for the DataZone session restriction; the current full aws_role edge is overbroad and CSPM lacks DataZone inventory. AWS AssociateEnvironmentRole, GetEnvironmentCredentials, GetEnvironment and ListProjectMemberships APIs.

exclusion_technique: Obtain the role credentials of an existing queue
review_evidence: The replacement joins ListFarms, ListQueues and GetQueue to one exact queue and attached IAM role. For a direct IAM caller it checks deadline:AssumeQueueRoleForUser on that queue ARN, target role trust for the exact farm, and known source guardrails. Unknown or missing joins do not create a definite edge. AWS Deadline API, service-role and permissions-overview docs; focused inventory and graph tests.

exclusion_technique: Register a logical worker on an existing customer-managed fleet and vend its fleet role
review_evidence: The replacement joins an existing active customer-managed fleet, capacity and exact role to broad CreateWorker, AssumeFleetRoleForWorker and dependent ListTagsForResource/TagResource grants for generated worker IDs, plus farm-scoped role trust. Worker credentials grant Deadline worker access; unrelated attached fleet-role policies are not assumed effective. Focused positive and negative tests cover IAM scope and fleet prerequisites.

exclusion_technique: Replace the content of a custom test specification used by privileged runs
review_evidence: AWS UpdateUpload(editContent=true) can replace an existing custom test specification; Device Farm runs its commands with the run or project execution role. An IAM role edge requires the exact upload ARN, a compatible run or schedulable project/device/app/test package, and that run's effective role. The current privesc collector does not join the edited upload to a future or source-startable run and role, so UpdateUpload alone must not report impersonation. AWS UpdateUpload, ScheduleRun, test-spec and execution-role docs. Follow-up inventory now records exact project-bound upload and pool metadata without signed URLs; it does not yet prove a source-startable matching run and role, so this remains a candidate.

exclusion_technique: Schedule SSM command documents on tagged instances through DLM pre/post scripts
review_evidence: DLM CreateLifecyclePolicy plus iam:PassRole can run an eligible SSM Command document through a DLM service role on a tagged managed EC2 instance. An AWS principal-to-principal route requires exact same-Region policy/target tags, usable document and DLM role SendCommand/DescribeDocument/GetDocument authorization, running managed instance, its mapped IAM instance-profile role and greater reachable authority. Existing DLM/SSM/EC2 inventories are partial; do not report an edge from PassRole alone (AWS DLM pre/post-script flow).

exclusion_technique: Reset the password of a directory user with Management Console access
review_evidence: ResetUserPassword on an exact Managed Microsoft AD or Simple AD directory can set a user's password, but a path to a particular IAM role needs that exact directory user, a collected console-role assignment and usable console sign-in. The current collector has directory metadata but no user-to-role join. AWS ResetUserPassword and directory console access guides.

exclusion_technique: Reset the password of the built-in directory administrator
review_evidence: AWS creates a named Admin user in a Managed Microsoft AD directory under its customer OU, and ResetUserPassword can reset that user's password; Simple AD also excepts its administrator from the privileged-group reset restriction. The old exclusion's claim that the admin subject is inherently unknown is too broad. An exact directory-principal target still needs directory identity/type, active state and a directory-scoped target node rather than the current account-wide domain-admin placeholder; AWS ResetUserPassword and What gets created with Managed Microsoft AD guides.

DeleteResourcePolicy removes the policy from one DynamoDB table or stream. It can remove a resource-level Deny, but that only changes access to that resource for an identity that has another applicable Allow; it does not yield credentials or privileges of another AWS principal. The old aws_verified_authority target did not identify a second principal or a specific newly effective action. Keep outside the requested principal-to-principal catalog; AWS DynamoDB resource-policy authorization and DeleteResourcePolicy API docs.

exclusion_technique: Replace the root volume of an existing role-bearing EC2 instance
review_evidence: CreateReplaceRootVolumeTask may boot an existing role-bearing instance from a replacement AMI or snapshot, but the EC2 write alone does not prove that attacker code is on the replacement root volume or will execute. Join an exact source-controlled compatible image, instance state and profile role, effective task permission, boot path and credential exposure before restoring; EC2 Replace Root Volume documentation.

DescribeLaunchTemplateVersions can disclose user data from an exact template version, but that data may contain no usable IAM access key. A principal edge needs safe inspection of a specific version, credential presence and validity, its AWS subject and added effective permissions; listing a template or seeing user data does not establish these facts.

exclusion_technique: Add a role to an instance profile used by an instance the source controls
review_evidence: AddRoleToInstanceProfile plus PassRole can place a role into an empty profile, or replace one after RemoveRoleFromInstanceProfile. The source still needs a specific controlled instance using that profile, or authority to associate the profile with one, and a working path to its credentials. Join exact profile occupancy, instance association, host control and effective grants before restoring; IAM and EC2 profile docs.

exclusion_technique: Launch an instance that joins an ECS cluster to receive task roles
review_evidence: RunInstances with an ECS-capable instance profile and controlled bootstrap may register a new host to a named cluster, but ECS task roles are not assigned just because the host joins. Need exact agent startup, cluster membership, task placement and target task role plus source access to that host. Without those joins this is the instance-profile role route, not an additional task-role edge; ECS EC2 launch documentation.

exclusion_technique: Map a trusted private repository prefix (or ROOT) to an upstream the source controls
review_evidence: A pull-through-cache rule can redirect cache misses under its prefix to a supported upstream, but an existing repository is not replaced. Need an exact absent repository, attacker-controlled upstream image path, matching workload image reference, pull boundary, workload role and effective rule-creation prerequisites before an AWS role edge; ECR pull-through-cache documentation.

Pull rights can expose image layers, but the page gives no specific image containing a usable AWS credential or its IAM subject and added authority. ECR authentication only carries the caller's existing ECR permissions. Restore a principal edge only if image content is safely inspected and an exact usable credential and additional IAM authority are established.

exclusion_technique: Push to an ECR Public repository consumed by workloads with roles
review_evidence: ECR Public image write can become code execution for a workload that later pulls the changed tag. The old YAML did not join an exact public image and mutable tag to a workload role, refresh boundary and effective publisher permission; unknown external consumers cannot be assigned an AWS principal edge. Collect these facts before restoring.

exclusion_technique: Rewrite an ECR Public repository policy to grant the source push access
review_evidence: A repository policy could grant the source image-push actions and enable a later poisoned tag. This is not the workload role by itself. Need an exact repository, effective policy-write grant, policy capability, matching mutable image tag and later consumer role and pull boundary; account and service restrictions must be evaluated.

exclusion_technique: Push an image over a mutable tag consumed by a workload with a role
review_evidence: PutImage can replace a mutable tag with an attacker-controlled image, but Lambda pins the digest until update and ECS normally resolves on deployment. The App Runner automatic-deployment case is now restored as aws-apprunner-mutable-ecr-autodeploy with exact same-account repository, watched mutable tag, full push grants and service role. Other consumers such as ECS and Lambda still require their own refresh and role joins; ECR and workload documentation.

exclusion_technique: Make an immutable repository mutable and overwrite a consumed tag
review_evidence: PutImageTagMutability can enable overwriting an immutable tag, but alone provides neither image content nor execution. Join effective mutability-change and push permissions on the same repository to an exact tag, attacker-controlled content, consuming workload role and refresh boundary; inspect exclusion filters and repository policy before a role edge.

exclusion_technique: Rewrite the registry policy to grant the source push access to all repositories
review_evidence: Registry policy scope and permitted actions depend on the account's registry policy version. A policy change may enable image-related rights, but not automatically execution under a workload role. Verify actual scope, effective policy, exact image tag, consumer, refresh boundary and role; distinguish replication or cache import from ordinary PutImage rights.

exclusion_technique: Rewrite a private repository policy to grant the source push access
review_evidence: A repository policy can grant the source image-push actions, but that only creates a path to image mutation. Need an exact repository and effective policy-write grant, account and policy restrictions, mutable tag, content-push capability, matching consumer image and later refresh under a known role before claiming principal escalation.

exclusion_technique: Move a service onto a capacity provider backed by instances the source controls
review_evidence: Changing a capacity provider and service strategy does not itself put a victim task on a source-controlled host. An exact route needs a source-controlled live EC2/ASG host, provider-to-cluster association, service strategy accepting that provider, placement of a specific task and its recorded task role. Current collector has task and container-instance data but no complete ASG/provider ownership and future-placement join. Candidate.

exclusion_technique: Drain or deregister legitimate container instances so service tasks are replaced onto a controlled instance
review_evidence: Drain or deregister can make a replica service replace tasks, but a source-owned connected host with compatible capacity and placement constraints must receive the exact replacement task. Need same-cluster host ownership, service/task placement, role and effective drain or deregister grant. Scheduler choice is not guaranteed by the permission alone. Candidate.

exclusion_technique: Schedule attacker-controlled ECS code under a task role
review_evidence: EventBridge can launch an ECS task on a schedule, but a role-less task gives no target role. Need an exact attacker-controlled task definition naming the task role, caller permission to install the rule target and pass the EventBridge invocation role, and that invocation role's RunTask and PassRole rights for the exact task and task role. AWS ECS EventBridge IAM-role and task-definition docs confirm separate invocation and task roles; current generic challenge fact has no such joins.

exclusion_technique: Execute commands in a running ECS task with ECS Exec
review_evidence: Restored as active aws-ecs-executecommand. ECS DescribeTasks projection now retains only container name/state and ExecuteCommandAgent name/state, without environment or agent error details. The precondition joins one RUNNING task and target task role, enabled Exec and a RUNNING agent in the selected container; it checks source ExecuteCommand on both exact cluster and task and all four target-role SSM channel permissions. Configured Exec KMS encryption requires source GenerateDataKey and target Decrypt; unknown or denied prerequisites cannot yield a role edge. Twelve focused positive, negative and unresolved cases pass, including unsupported read-only root containers.

exclusion_technique: Register a controlled instance into a cluster and let the scheduler place tasks on it
review_evidence: RegisterContainerInstance needs a live ECS agent on a source-controlled host; an instance identity document/signature or registration API grant alone does not supply connected capacity. A scheduled victim task must actually land on that host and expose its role there. Need host ownership, agentConnected, cluster/capacity placement and target task role joins. Candidate.

exclusion_technique: Register a controlled instance into a cluster and steer tasks onto it
review_evidence: A direct StartTask call can name a container instance, but the caller needs a connected source-controlled host, an active task definition compatible with that capacity, required PassRole grants and the exact target task role. Registration alone cannot serve the agent channel or yield credentials. Candidate for same-host and task-definition joins.

exclusion_technique: Associate an attacker-controlled OIDC identity provider with an EKS cluster that binds a privileged RBAC group
review_evidence: AWS AssociateIdentityProviderConfig adds OIDC authentication to an exact EKS cluster, not IAM or Kubernetes authorization. A usable Kubernetes-admin step needs an attacker-controlled reachable issuer, valid token claims and audience, and an existing RoleBinding/ClusterRoleBinding whose effective group matches the configured group claim and prefix. To reach another AWS principal, additionally join Kubernetes permissions to a specific workload service account and its IRSA or Pod Identity role association, trust and effective role credentials; OIDC login alone is no AWS-role edge. Current CSPM lacks the RBAC/token/role chain, so retain as candidate and do not report a full IAM principal pivot from the API grant alone. AWS EKS external OIDC identity provider and AssociateIdentityProviderConfig docs.

exclusion_technique: Create an EKS access entry that places the source in an existing privileged Kubernetes group
review_evidence: CreateAccessEntry can place the source IAM principal in a custom Kubernetes group, but cluster-admin follows only if the same EKS cluster has a recorded ClusterRoleBinding for that group and the source can authenticate as the entry. Current AWS inventory has access entries but no joined Kubernetes RBAC subject. Candidate for an exact EKS-to-Kubernetes RBAC join; system: groups are rejected.

exclusion_technique: Bind a passable role to a Kubernetes service account through EKS Pod Identity
review_evidence: CreatePodIdentityAssociation and PassRole bind a role to a namespace/service account, but a role pivot requires source control of a pod running under that exact service account, Pod Identity Agent readiness, the target role trust, and permission to read its credentials. The CSPM has association inventory but lacks the pod-control join. Candidate.

exclusion_technique: Create a managed node group with a passed node role
review_evidence: CreateNodegroup plus PassRole causes EKS to launch nodes with the role, but the caller does not receive the node credentials merely by creating the group. Need a source-controlled node bootstrap/launch-template path and scheduled workload or local access to that exact node. Fargate profile creation likewise does not grant caller execution-role credentials. Candidate.

exclusion_technique: Rewrite the Kubernetes groups of an existing EKS access entry
review_evidence: UpdateAccessEntry can replace groups on an existing entry. Need the exact access entry to name a principal controlled by the source and the same cluster RBAC to bind the new custom group to useful permissions; the AWS access-entry inventory alone cannot prove that. Candidate for joined IAM and Kubernetes evidence.

exclusion_technique: Repoint an existing EKS Pod Identity association to another passable role
review_evidence: UpdatePodIdentityAssociation can replace an existing role binding, but an edge to that role needs an exact association, a pod/service account the source controls, Pod Identity Agent readiness, PassRole/GetRole and target trust. Current association inventory does not prove source pod control. Candidate.

TargetRoleArn can make Pod Identity chain from the association role into a cross-account role, but the caller must control a pod using that exact association and the first/target role policies and trust must allow chaining. A bare UpdatePodIdentityAssociation grant or target ARN is insufficient; candidate for exact pod, trust and permission joins.

exclusion_technique: Deploy an attacker-hosted application version to an existing environment
review_evidence: CreateApplicationVersion plus UpdateEnvironment can deploy a controlled source bundle to an existing environment, but the CSPM does not bind one application/version and readable same-Region S3 object to an exact ready environment, its EC2 instance profile and executable runtime. The collector retains environment metadata but omits IamInstanceProfile and running instance joins. Restore only after effective scoped grants and source-to-role execution are joined; AWS CreateApplicationVersion and UpdateEnvironment docs.

exclusion_technique: Replace an environment's source bundle in S3 and rebuild it
review_evidence: RebuildEnvironment recreates an environment from its deployed application version, so an overwrite matters only if that version reads the exact mutable S3 source object after replacement. Need the environment-to-version-to-object and instance-profile-role joins, effective PutObject and rebuild grants, object version behavior and executable payload witness. Rebuild can delete a coupled database; corrected the page's automatic-execution claim using AWS rebuild docs.

exclusion_technique: Inject runtime-influencing environment properties into an existing environment
review_evidence: UpdateEnvironment can set application environment properties without PassRole, but values such as NODE_OPTIONS only execute code if the actual application starts the matching runtime and the hook/module exists or a valid inline route applies. The collector discards these runtime properties and does not join the exact environment instance profile, platform/runtime or executable hook. Need those facts plus a refresh boundary and scoped permission before an IAM role edge.

exclusion_technique: Add steps to an existing EMR cluster
review_evidence: Exact active cluster ARN and collected EC2 instance profile joined to the attached IAM role and AddJobFlowSteps permission; positive and negative tests in tests/test_peaso_privesc_emr_existing_steps.py; AWS EMR API and command-runner documentation.

exclusion_technique: Overwrite an S3 bootstrap action or step script used by EMR
review_evidence: AWS EMR runs configured S3 bootstrap scripts during cluster creation and can run S3 step scripts; overwrite of the exact current object could execute under the cluster EC2 instance profile after the relevant trigger. Need exact object URI and effective write permission, a consuming bootstrap action or step, identified cluster profile and execution trigger. The EMR service role is separate. Current evaluator lacks the object-to-consumer-to-profile join, so bare PutObject is insufficient.

exclusion_technique: Attach to an active EMR Serverless Spark Connect session
review_evidence: GetSessionEndpoint returns a bearer token for an exact existing session without passing its execution role. A definite role edge needs the collected session ID, active state, its exact executionRoleArn, effective permission on that session ARN, usable endpoint connectivity and a stronger role than the source. Current collector inventories applications only, not sessions. AWS GetSessionEndpoint and Spark Connect docs.

exclusion_technique: Poison the default runtime configuration of an EMR Serverless application
review_evidence: UpdateApplication may plant Spark defaults that a later compatible job inherits, but requires a CREATED or STOPPED application, attacker-controlled readable S3 archive, job execution role and no job-level override of the injected defaults. Current collector does not join an application to later jobs, their exact roles and readable objects or runtime overrides. Do not infer code execution from UpdateApplication permission alone. AWS UpdateApplication and default-configs docs.

AWS ListTargetsByRule returns a target constant Input, HttpParameters and InputTransformer.InputTemplate, which could contain a complete AWS access-key tuple but usually contain only ordinary payload data or references. An IAM edge needs actual complete credential material, the access key ID bound to an exact different IAM user or role session, credential validity and additional effective authority; RoleArn and Secrets Manager ARNs alone are locators, not credentials. Current collector inventories target metadata but does not safely extract and verify secrets; keep as candidate rather than infer from ListTargetsByRule access. AWS ListTargetsByRule API.

AWS FIS supports aws:ssm:start-automation-execution and passes documentParameters through a stored experiment role. A collected template, exact Automation document content, permitted parameter values, its Automation role and a concrete IAM policy change could prove an exact target principal gain. The old full FIS-role target is overbroad; investigate a narrower route rather than claim it. AWS FIS Actions reference.

exclusion_technique: Open a running Managed Flink Studio notebook through a presigned URL
review_evidence: Exact running INTERACTIVE application ARN and collected ServiceExecutionRole joined to CreateApplicationPresignedUrl on the same application; positive and negative tests in tests/test_peaso_privesc_flink_existing_studio.py; AWS Flink API and Studio documentation.

exclusion_technique: Repoint the code of an existing Managed Flink application that keeps its execution role
review_evidence: DescribeApplication can bind an application to its exact ServiceExecutionRole, now retained by collector projection. A definite route also needs a writable code artifact readable by that role and an execution transition; the current inventory omits the S3 code pointer, so UpdateApplication alone cannot establish role reach.

exclusion_technique: Open a Session Manager shell on a GameLift fleet compute and use its instance role
review_evidence: Implemented the bounded EC2 shared-credential route. The collector joins an active fleet with its exact InstanceRoleArn, SHARED_CREDENTIAL_FILE setting and an active listed compute; the evaluator requires effective GetComputeAccess on that fleet ARN. It reports a conditional edge because shell access and file readability still occur at runtime. Default SDK credential flow and container fleets remain outside this entry. AWS GetComputeAccess, FleetAttributes and GameLift shared credentials documentation; focused positive and negative checks.

exclusion_technique: Overwrite the S3 script or dependency of an existing Glue job
review_evidence: The exact ScriptLocation object subset is implemented by aws-glue-overwrite-existing-job-script: collected job, role, source PutObject, role GetObject and same-job StartJobRun or active schedule are joined, with positive and negative tests. The retired label also covered dependency-object replacement; that distinct subset still needs exact collected dependency URI, runtime loading and a bound execution path before the combined retired row can be signed off. AWS Glue JobCommand and script editor docs. Glue argument precedence is checked: pinned --scriptLocation is unresolved, and scheduled runs require no script redirect in job defaults or trigger action arguments; only argument names are retained.

exclusion_technique: Grant a controlled Identity Center identity Grafana administrator access
review_evidence: UpdatePermissions can grant Grafana ADMIN to a specified Identity Center user or group, but this is workspace authority rather than IAM role credentials. A definite service-plane edge requires the exact workspace, AWS_SSO configuration, effective scoped grant, a valid controlled directory identity, successful per-item response and sign-in path; current CSPM has no directory subject-to-source join. AWS UpdatePermissions API documents item-level errors.

exclusion_technique: Deploy a malicious Greengrass component to core devices and use their token exchange role
review_evidence: AWS documents executable Greengrass components and a device-specific nucleus iotRoleAlias pointing through IoT to the token exchange IAM role. Need effective component/deployment rights, the exact recipient core device and execution, its role alias and IoT policy, alias target role and token exchange service. Current evaluator lacks those joins; trust in credentials.iot.amazonaws.com is not enough to select a role.

HealthOmics CreateWorkflow can record a definitionZip value in a CloudTrail event, but the logged value does not establish that the workflow ZIP contains a usable AWS credential or name the credential subject. Reading CloudTrail records therefore grants event data, not another IAM principal. The CSPM does not decode customer workflow archives or validate credentials. AWS HealthOmics CloudTrail logging guide.

exclusion_technique: Start a HealthOmics workflow run with a passed service role
review_evidence: A new private workflow can contain a source-controlled definition ZIP, and StartRun names the target service role; this may run code under that role. Need exact CreateWorkflow and StartRun effective grants on generated workflow/run resources, same-account PassRole and omics trust, runnable container image/ECR access, output and run readiness before restoring. AWS CreateWorkflow, StartRun and HealthOmics container docs.

exclusion_technique: Register an OIDC provider that a role trusts but that no longer exists
review_evidence: CreateOpenIDConnectProvider registers an issuer URL and audiences, but neither the missing provider ARN nor the IAM grant proves control of that issuer or possession of a signed token whose audience and subject match the target role trust. AWS documents the provider registration and trust relationship (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/APIReference/API_CreateOpenIDConnectProvider.html) and requires matching token claims for federation (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_create_for-idp_oidc.html). No AWS IAM inventory fact joins the source principal to issuer-controlled tokens, so this cannot be an exact AWS principal-to-principal edge.

exclusion_technique: Create a role in a trusted account to satisfy another account's role trust
review_evidence: AWS IAM does not allow a partial wildcard in a role Principal; a trust that delegates to a trusted account and filters aws:PrincipalArn can match a future role ARN under the named path. A directly named role Principal is converted to an immutable principal ID and cannot be satisfied merely by recreating its ARN. The source would need CreateRole on one unoccupied matching ARN, control of its trust so it can assume the new role, PutRolePolicy or another exact grant of sts:AssumeRole on the cross-account target to that same new role, and an effective source-to-new-role assumption path. The target trust, explicit denies, boundaries and SCPs must all be evaluated against the new role, not the existing source. Current YAML has no synthetic new-role-to-target join; candidate remains. AWS Principal element and cross-account evaluation guides.

exclusion_technique: Register an attacker-chosen audience on an OIDC provider that roles trust
review_evidence: AddClientIDToOpenIDConnectProvider only adds an audience to an existing provider (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/APIReference/API_AddClientIDToOpenIDConnectProvider.html). It neither issues a signed token nor changes a role trust's subject conditions; AWS requires matching federation claims (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_create_for-idp_oidc.html). AWS inventory cannot establish that the source principal can obtain a token from that exact issuer with the new audience and allowed subject, so the IAM grant alone is not an exact principal-to-principal edge.

exclusion_technique: Replace or remove the permissions boundary of the source role
review_evidence: PutRolePermissionsBoundary can replace the source role boundary and unlock existing identity-policy grants only when the replacement policy and before/after effective permissions are known. AWS says a changed role boundary takes effect on the next assumption; the source needs a verified way to obtain another session for that exact role. The current session alone is insufficient. Keep candidate until exact boundary, new permission, request-condition and reacquisition joins are established; AWS Update permissions for a role and PutRolePermissionsBoundary docs.

exclusion_technique: Replace or remove the permissions boundary of the source user
review_evidence: AWS confirms PutUserPermissionsBoundary replaces the user boundary but grants nothing on its own. Need exact current boundary, replacement managed policy, existing identity grants, and before/after effective permission comparison to prove an added action; the old account-admin target is unjustified without this. AWS PutUserPermissionsBoundary docs.

exclusion_technique: Replace or remove the permissions boundary of a role the source can assume
review_evidence: Changing an assumable role boundary may expose previously capped identity grants, but AWS says the new boundary takes effect when the role is next assumed. Require effective PutRolePermissionsBoundary on the exact target role and replacement policy, trust plus effective sts:AssumeRole for the source, a fresh session, and a specific before/after permission gain. Do not infer administrator access from boundary-write permission alone; AWS Update permissions for a role and PutRolePermissionsBoundary docs.

exclusion_technique: Move one of the source's groups into an IAM path where it can edit group policies
review_evidence: UpdateGroup can change a group's path and therefore its ARN. Need effective authorization for the path change, source membership in that exact group, policy-write permission on the post-move ARN, and a demonstrated new effective permission. AWS explicitly requires grants on both old and new names for a rename, but does not clearly specify that the same rule applies to a path-only change (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/APIReference/API_UpdateGroup.html); do not silently impose that extra requirement and create a false negative.

exclusion_technique: Move the source user into an IAM path where it can edit user policies
review_evidence: UpdateUser can change the source user's path and therefore its ARN. Need effective authorization for the path change, policy-write permission on the post-move ARN, and a demonstrated new effective permission.
