AWS explicitly requires grants on both old and new names for a rename, but does not clearly specify that the same rule applies to a path-only change (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/APIReference/API_UpdateUser.html); do not silently impose that extra requirement and create a false negative.

exclusion_technique: Add an Identity Center user controlled by the source to a group
review_evidence: CreateGroupMembership can add a specific Identity Center user to a group that has an account assignment. A role edge needs the exact group-to-permission-set/account assignment and proof the source controls that user and can sign in; group membership alone grants the source IAM principal no role session. Candidate for identity-control and assignment joins (AWS CreateGroupMembership API).

exclusion_technique: Create an Identity Center user and assign it a permission set
review_evidence: CreateUser plus CreateAccountAssignment can assign a new directory user an account permission set; new user creation alone does not establish portal login or source control. Need native-directory instance, exact new user, CreateAccountAssignment scope, usable login/password or controlled mailbox, permission set and provisioned role join. Candidate self-controlled user path (AWS CreateUser and CreateAccountAssignment APIs).

exclusion_technique: Create an Identity Center user and add it to a privileged group
review_evidence: CreateUser plus CreateGroupMembership can place a new directory user into a group with an account assignment. Need the exact group, assignment, permission set, account and a source-controlled working login for the new user; an external-IdP directory may not accept local password setup. Candidate (AWS CreateUser and CreateGroupMembership APIs).

Keyspaces GetRecords returns row mutations from a named CDC stream, possibly including the captured columns. Neither stream metadata nor read permission identifies a complete AWS credential, its IAM subject or added authority. The CSPM reads no customer stream records or validates leaked credentials. This is data access, so no exact principal-to-principal edge follows. AWS Keyspaces CDC and GetRecords docs.

cassandra:Select reads rows in an authorized Keyspaces table; CQL clients may also need Select on system tables. A table permission or schema does not establish that a row contains a usable AWS credential, its principal or added authority. The CSPM reads no customer rows or validates credentials. This is data access rather than an identifiable IAM principal pivot. AWS Keyspaces IAM policy examples and CQL SELECT docs.

GetDurableExecutionHistory with IncludeExecutionData can return step inputs, results and callbacks for an exact execution; a customer-managed KMS key also requires caller kms:Decrypt. No API field proves those values contain AWS credentials. A role edge needs actual complete usable credentials, a verified AWS subject and added authority. CSPM does not collect execution payloads or validate credential subjects, so keep excluded.

GetFunction can return a ZIP download location or image URI, but a package may contain no usable AWS credential. A principal edge needs safe content inspection, exact credential subject and successful effective authority beyond the caller; package access alone is data exposure. Candidate.

ListFunctions returns a subset of FunctionConfiguration including Environment.Variables, but a listed value may be a reference, non-AWS secret or unusable credential. Need safe review of the actual returned value, exact IAM subject and added authority, with any KMS restrictions evaluated. Candidate for strict credential-content proof; AWS ListFunctions API.

ListVersionsByFunction can return version-specific Environment.Variables, including historical values, but listing alone does not establish another AWS principal. Need the exact function version and returned credential value safely verified as usable for a named IAM subject with added authority. Candidate for strict version-content proof; AWS ListVersionsByFunction API.

exclusion_technique: Open a shell into a running Lambda MicroVM
review_evidence: CreateMicrovmShellAuthToken can open a shell only on a recorded running MicroVM of the authorized image with SHELL_INGRESS and a reachable endpoint; reaching another IAM role additionally needs that runtime executionRoleArn and usable credentials. The CSPM collects image summaries but not exact live runtimes, connectors and role attachments. Candidate for a runtime-to-image/role join.

exclusion_technique: Cross-account resource sharing matrix (S3, KMS, Secrets Manager, SNS/SQS, RAM, snapshots, models, ...)
review_evidence: UpdateFunctionConfiguration can set AWS_LAMBDA_EXEC_WRAPPER or attach a code-bearing layer without passing a new role, but execution needs a compatible existing ZIP function, a wrapper file that actually exists in a readable layer or package, and a later invocation. Current active role-swap route requires PassRole and code update, so it does not cover this configuration-only path. Candidate for exact wrapper/layer and role join.

AWS GetSession returns conversation state and application session attributes for a Lex bot, not IAM or STS credentials. Another user's Lex session ID is an application identifier, not another AWS principal. A particular application could store an AWS secret in session data, but that would need separately verified content and subject evidence. Generic session disclosure stays outside the principal graph; AWS Lex session guide.

Lightsail IMDS exposes instance and user-data metadata, but the Lightsail inventory does not identify a customer IAM role or its credentials on a named instance; AWS states Lightsail does not support service roles. EC2 IAM instance-profile documentation cannot be applied to a Lightsail host by name alone. A real, separately verified credential would need its subject and added authority before a principal edge. AWS Lightsail IMDS and IAM guides.

exclusion_technique: Run an attacker-selected ad-hoc S3 batch job in an existing M2 application
review_evidence: StartBatchJob accepts an S3 batch-job identifier for an existing deployed M2 application, so caller-chosen JCL or script can cross into that application. AWS documents that installed programs, engine and application definition control what it can execute; a JCL path alone does not prove arbitrary commands or use of the application IAM role. The CSPM has runtime-environment inventory for new-app deployment but no exact existing application, role, S3 job artifact, engine/runtime or usable command join. Keep this conditional candidate until those facts can bind source StartBatchJob to a target role. AWS M2 StartBatchJob, batch-job and application-definition docs.

exclusion_technique: Deploy a modified M2 application version under its existing role
review_evidence: AWS UpdateApplication creates a new stored version and cannot change the existing roleArn; GetApplication exposes that role and deployed version. A definite edge needs a valid attacker-controlled definition or executable artifact, the exact application and role, later CreateDeployment of that version to an eligible environment, and StartApplication if needed. Updating alone grants no role execution. CSPM has no M2 application inventory or version-to-deployment-to-role join, so the route remains excluded.

exclusion_technique: Mint an Airflow CLI token for an MWAA environment and run code as its execution role
review_evidence: CreateCliToken returns Airflow CLI access for one environment and can trigger an authorized existing DAG, but a fixed DAG does not prove attacker-chosen code or general access to the environment execution role. A definite role route needs the exact environment and role, reachable web server, token use allowed by Airflow, and a DAG with a proven controllable code-bearing input or separate writable DAG object. The S3 DAG-object route is implemented separately. AWS CreateCliToken and CLI access docs.

exclusion_technique: Mint an Airflow web-login token for an MWAA environment and run code as its execution role
review_evidence: CreateWebLoginToken is authorized on a specific Airflow RBAC role ARN, not merely an environment ARN; Viewer or Public grants do not become Admin. Even an Admin token requires reachable web server and an attacker-controlled executable DAG or proven code-bearing input before the environment's exact execution role is reached. The collector does not record Airflow DAG definitions or RBAC actions. AWS access-policy and CreateWebLoginToken docs.

exclusion_technique: Write a DAG file into an MWAA environment's DAG bucket and run code as its execution role
review_evidence: Restored as aws-mwaa-s3-putobject-dag in HackTricks Cloud and synced CSPM. The evaluator joins a collected AVAILABLE environment's ExecutionRoleArn, SourceBucketArn and DagS3Path with effective PutObject on a Python DAG object and the exact role's ListBucket/GetObject. Focused positive and wrong object, target role, read/list, status and denied-inventory negatives pass in tests/test_peaso_privesc_mwaa_existing_dag.py. AWS MWAA GetEnvironment and DAG synchronization docs; runtime synchronization remains conditional.

RegisterDelegatedAdministrator is a management-account operation granting service-specific delegation to a member account, not full AWS account administration. The member-account principal still needs service IAM permissions; IAM centralized root additionally needs root sessions enabled and explicit sts:AssumeRoot with an allowed task policy. Need the exact controlled member principal, service, configuration, member targets and before/after effective action to restore an authority edge; AWS Organizations API and IAM centralized root docs.

An ACM ACME external account binding associates an ACME client with one IAM role. AWS says ACM assumes that role only to authorize ACME certificate issue or revoke operations; the client receives EAB credentials, not STS role credentials or arbitrary role actions. This can be a certificate-issuance risk but is not a principal-to-principal role session. Verified exclusion from AWS principal-to-principal YAML; AWS External account bindings and IAM for ACME guides.

exclusion_technique: Change CDKToolkit TrustedAccounts to attacker account and deploy role trust
review_evidence: Generic challenge evidence does not prove control of the cross-account subject admitted by bootstrap trust.

AWS RDS Proxy auth secrets contain backend database usernames and passwords, not IAM role credentials. DescribeDBProxies plus GetSecretValue may expose database access, while end-to-end IAM authentication may use no backend password secret. Keep this database credential issue outside the AWS principal-to-principal catalog; the retired aws_role target was an overclaim. AWS RDS Proxy credential setup and connecting docs.

PutResourcePolicy on an owner-account primary key can grant bounded key operations to a named external IAM principal, but cross-account use also requires that principal's identity-policy Allow. The key-owner caller gains neither the external principal's credentials nor its authority; self-grant changes the same principal's resource access. No source-controlled second principal is identified, so this is key sharing rather than principal-to-principal escalation. AWS Payment Cryptography resource-policy docs.

PutResourcePolicy can grant a same-account principal bounded use of one primary payment key without a separate identity allow; the page documents a valid self-grant. It does not provide another role session, but a controlled alternate principal or exact new key operation may warrant a scoped permission-gain route. Keep as a candidate pending resource, subject, deny and key-state joins.

exclusion_technique: Publish a malicious certificate template through PCA Connector for AD and enroll as a domain admin
review_evidence: CreateTemplate stores a certificate template for a connected Active Directory. AWS requires a subject or SAN option derived from AD; the retired empty SubjectNameFlags example cannot establish an arbitrary requester-supplied UPN. A certificate, eligible AD requester and domain-controller mapping are separate steps. Even a successful AD authentication would be an AD identity, not an identified AWS IAM principal. Verified exclusion from AWS principal-to-principal YAML; AWS Create a connector template guide and HackTricks Cloud PCA Connector page.

exclusion_technique: Weaken an existing PCA Connector for AD certificate template in place
review_evidence: UpdateTemplate replaces certificate-template settings but neither enrolls a certificate nor grants an AWS IAM role. Any AD impersonation depends on an eligible requester, issued certificate and domain-controller mapping; the page names no AWS federated-role trust from that AD identity. Verified exclusion from AWS principal-to-principal YAML while retaining the AD risk documentation; AWS connector-template guide and HackTricks Cloud PCA Connector page.

GetCluster exposes the exact cluster secret ARN (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/pcs/latest/userguide/working-with_clusters_secrets_find_pcs.html), but AWS describes that secret as a Slurm scheduler authentication key, including JWT signing for the REST API, not AWS IAM credentials (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/pcs/latest/userguide/working-with_clusters_secrets.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/pcs/latest/userguide/slurm-rest-api-authenticate.html). Scheduler access and a subsequent job would still need private network reachability, a usable Slurm identity, job execution, an exact node role, and credential exposure. The secret read alone is no AWS principal-to-principal edge; the old inferred node-role edge remains excluded.

exclusion_technique: Create a Parallel Computing Service (PCS) compute node group with a passed instance profile
review_evidence: AWS PCS requires the selected instance-profile role to have an AWSPCS name or /aws-pcs/ path and pcs:RegisterComputeNodeGroupInstance. CreateComputeNodeGroup plus PassRole can launch nodes with that profile, but it does not give the IAM caller a Slurm login or a way to submit code; AWS job submission uses sbatch from a reachable login node. The collector does not join a controlled scheduler/login foothold, exact cluster/queue and node group, or launch readiness. Keep candidate rather than assert target-role execution; AWS PCS instance-profile, minimum-permission and run-job guides.

Partner Central CreateEngagementInvitation shares Engagement snapshots with another connected Partner account after acceptance. The recipient is a Partner application membership, not an IAM user/role, and the operation does not confer another AWS principal's IAM actions. Retain as Partner Central data-sharing persistence, outside principal-to-principal IAM escalation (HackTricks source section).

aps:PutResourcePolicy on an exact AMP workspace can name a controlled IAM principal and grant bounded Prometheus query/ingest APIs, not general workspace management. Require the exact source mutation grant, workspace/Region, target principal and effective recipient authorization, including cross-account identity allow where applicable (AWS AMP resource-policy announcement and IAM cross-account policy evaluation).

kafka:PutClusterPolicy can grant a named external IAM principal bounded cluster access. Require exact cluster/Region, IAM authentication and policy actions, recipient identity allow, VPC connectivity and intended Kafka data-plane grant; policy permission alone does not prove broker reachability or a broader IAM role (AWS MSK cross-account cluster-policy guide).

Q Business CreateDataAccessor can grant SearchRelevantContent to a supported registered ISV IAM role, but arbitrary external AWS principals are not eligible. Require eligible ISV role/tenant, application and index, resource policy, Identity Center assignment, user authorization and exact resulting action; do not infer usable access from CreateDataAccessor alone (AWS Q Business data-accessor guide).

After consortium approval, CreateMember makes a Fabric network member owned by the external account. Its peer/CA identity is scoped to that blockchain network, not an IAM role in the victim account; retention of network access is a bounded persistence effect (HackTricks Managed Blockchain persistence page).

mediaconnect:GrantFlowEntitlements can allow a selected AWS subscriber account to create a same-Region flow sourcing a transport-stream flow; entitlement is one-use and only bounded MediaConnect content access. Require exact flow/Region, enabled entitlement, controlled subscriber, recipient CreateFlow rights and a usable source; no IAM role takeover follows (AWS MediaConnect entitlement guide).

mediapackagev2:PutChannelPolicy on an exact channel can grant PutObject to a named IAM principal or IP-scoped wildcard principal. Original wildcard example is an IP-restricted ingest exposure, not anonymous AWS authority. Require exact channel ARN without /*, named recipient and cross-account identity allow for a principal edge, or keep the wildcard case as service exposure (AWS MediaPackage ingest authorization and policy ARN requirements).

CreateAccessor returns a BillingToken usable for AMB Ethereum/Polygon node API requests owned by the account. AWS documents that it authenticates those blockchain requests, not general IAM API calls or another IAM principal. Retain as service credential persistence (AWS AMB token access guide).

payment-cryptography:PutResourcePolicy on a primary key can grant a named external IAM role bounded cryptographic operations; the external role must also allow the action in its identity policy. Require exact key/Region, primary-key state, role/principal, matching recipient allow and action; key access is not general IAM role access (AWS Payment Cryptography resource-policy guide).

mediapackagev2:PutOriginEndpointPolicy can grant GetObject/GetHeadObject on one exact endpoint to a named IAM principal or anonymously via wildcard principal. Require exact endpoint ARN without /* and effective recipient authorization for an IAM edge; original wildcard case is public content exposure, not principal takeover (AWS MediaPackage origin authorization and policy ARN requirements).

ram:CreateResourceShare or AssociateResourceShare can share an exact Cloud WAN core network with another account or IAM principal. Require exact resource/share/principal, accepted invitation where required, live managed RAM permission, recipient attachment rights and network policy; the share gives bounded attachment authority, not general IAM actions or assured reachability (AWS RAM shareable resources and Cloud WAN sharing guide).

PassRole lets Pipes assume a role only for supported source, enrichment and target operations; a configured pipe neither yields role credentials nor arbitrary API execution. Exact downstream effect requires a pipe configuration, source access validated after creation, effective enrichment/target grants and records to process. AWS Pipes creation, execution-role and error-handling docs.

AWS StartPipe takes only the name of an existing pipe and no request body. It resumes the stored source, enrichment, target and role; the response contains pipe metadata, not role credentials. Any later action depends on eligible records and the preconfigured target, so StartPipe alone is bounded workflow invocation, not a principal-to-principal edge. The HackTricks Cloud page already states these limits. AWS StartPipe API and EventBridge Pipes permissions guide.

A Q Business data accessor gives a registered ISV role bounded SearchRelevantContent access to a customer application/index after accessor, policy/assignment and identity context setup. The customer-side caller does not receive or control that ISV role. This may share sensitive index data across accounts, but no source-to-role credential or authority path is established. AWS Q Business data-accessor docs.

exclusion_technique: Promote a controlled QuickSight user to ADMIN
review_evidence: Restored exact self-promotion route. Active QuickSight IAM User PrincipalId must equal federated/iam/<source IAM UserId> or federated-iam-<source IAM UserId>; same account and Region, active IAM-compatible subscription, non-admin role, no custom permission restriction, and effective UpdateUser on the exact QuickSight user ARN are required. Positive and negative route tests cover identity, resource, state, type, custom permissions, and subscription. AWS User PrincipalId example, UpdateUser API and service authorization reference.

AddRoleToDBCluster plus PassRole can associate an exact role with an existing Aurora cluster, but no general role session follows. A role edge needs the cluster engine, supported feature, role trust and effective permissions, database authentication, SQL privilege, and an exact integration operation that grants additional AWS authority; RDS AddRoleToDBCluster and Aurora integration docs.

AddRoleToDBInstance plus PassRole can associate a role with a supported available DB instance, but the source does not thereby obtain role credentials. Need exact instance/engine/feature, role trust and effective permissions, database login and SQL access to a supported integration before a bounded authority edge; RDS AddRoleToDBInstance docs.

exclusion_technique: Create an RDS Custom instance with a passed AWSRDSCustom instance profile
review_evidence: CreateDBInstance can choose an AWSRDSCustom instance profile under the documented name, trust and KMS constraints. The source still needs a supported host-access or code-execution path to obtain the EC2 role credentials. No exact profile-to-access foothold is collected, so creation plus PassRole alone is insufficient; RDS Custom documentation.

rds-db:connect can authenticate to a configured Aurora DB user only when IAM DB authentication and the engine user are ready, the resource ID matches and the endpoint is reachable. A role association or extension name alone does not prove an operation using that role. Need exact SQL rights, active associated role, configured integration and role-permitted AWS operation; RDS IAM DB auth and Aurora integration docs.

IAM database authentication gives a database session, not the full permissions of an RDS associated IAM role. Need an exact DB user and rds-db:connect resource, enabled IAM auth, reachability, SQL rights, active associated role and configured integration exposing an additional AWS action; RDS IAM DB auth docs.

GetSecretValue on the exact RDS-managed master secret may give a database login when decryption and network access also work, but not an IAM role session. Need exact secret-to-database and active-role joins plus configured integration, SQL rights and a role-permitted AWS operation; RDS managed master secret and Aurora integration docs.

ModifyDBCluster may reset a cluster master password when RDS does not manage it through Secrets Manager. Password control still needs database reachability or a supported Data API path and a usable SQL integration to exercise any associated role. Need exact cluster state, role, feature and added AWS operation; RDS ModifyDBCluster and Data API docs.

ModifyDBInstance may reset a non-Aurora instance master password when RDS is not managing it. This gives potential database access, not the associated IAM role session. Need exact instance state, network route, SQL integration, active associated role and role-permitted operation before an authority edge; RDS ModifyDBInstance docs.

GetClusterCredentials returns a short-lived password for a named Redshift database user, not STS credentials for the cluster IAM role. The user gains only recorded SQL grants; any AWS-backed SQL action needs separate database privilege and associated IAM role evidence. No general other-principal AWS role edge follows from this call. AWS IAM database authentication guide.

GetClusterCredentialsWithIAM derives a Redshift database identity from the caller and returns SQL credentials, not another IAM role's STS credentials. Database rights depend on that mapped user and its SQL grants. No full AWS role edge follows from the API alone. AWS Redshift IAM database authentication guide.

ModifyCluster master password changes a Redshift database login. A database superuser may gain SQL administration, but the operation neither issues STS credentials nor transfers the cluster's IAM roles to the caller. AWS-backed SQL integrations still require their own role, SQL privilege and action-specific proof. AWS Redshift role and ASSUMEROLE docs.

ModifyClusterIamRoles or UpdateNamespace plus iam:PassRole can associate an exact role with a Redshift warehouse, but association alone does not yield its credentials. A definite bounded AWS action needs the warehouse and role join, Redshift service trust, effective scoped grants, a database login with SQL and ASSUMEROLE rights, and a specific supported SQL integration/action. Preserve as a candidate for precise service-mediated authority, not a full role edge. AWS Redshift role and ASSUMEROLE docs.

Redshift Serverless GetCredentials returns a temporary password for the IAM-mapped database user, not credentials for the namespace's IAM role. Its rights are SQL grants and database-role mappings; a separate AWS-backed SQL operation would need exact authorization evidence. No full other-principal AWS role edge follows from token vending alone. AWS Redshift Serverless GetCredentials API.

exclusion_technique: Remove a certificate attribute mapping that a negative role-trust condition relies on
review_evidence: DeleteAttributeMapping or PutAttributeMapping can remove a mapped x509 tag from a profile, changing a role trust with a negative or IfExists condition. The route only works with a source-held valid certificate, enabled anchor/profile, exact listed role, and a trust statement where absence makes the condition true. Candidate for exact before/after mapping and trust/certificate join; a broad action grant is insufficient (AWS DeleteAttributeMapping API and Roles Anywhere trust model).

exclusion_technique: Remove the session-policy restriction of an IAM Roles Anywhere profile
review_evidence: UpdateProfile can remove or replace inline/managed session restrictions on a profile without changing its roleArns. Reaching the listed role also requires source possession of a valid private key/certificate, enabled matching anchor/profile, successful role trust, and proof the old policy withheld rights; the API grant alone cannot show those facts. Candidate for exact profile/certificate/effective-rights join (AWS UpdateProfile API).

CreateWorkspaceServiceAccountToken alone can mint a bearer token for a known existing ADMIN Grafana service account. The active catalog route requires both CreateWorkspaceServiceAccount and token creation, so this narrower path is missing. Need exact service account ID and recorded ADMIN role, eligible workspace, effective token permission and endpoint access before a definite Grafana authority edge; this is not IAM role credentials. AWS token API.

An MSK SASL/SCRAM secret stores a Kafka username and password. Reading it may enable broker authentication only with network access and matching Kafka ACLs; it does not reveal IAM or STS credentials or the authority of another AWS principal. The source page now lives in MSK post-exploitation; keep this data-plane credential exposure out of the principal graph. AWS MSK sign-in credential docs.

AddPermission grants a caller or service bounded invoke access to an existing function; it does not itself expose the function role. A principal edge requires an exact target whose existing code lets that caller obtain role credentials or perform a role-permitted privileged operation. Function ARN, policy effect and executable behavior are not joined. Candidate for a concrete consumer path.

Exposing an existing NONE-auth function URL makes its current behavior callable publicly, but URL reachability is not Lambda execution-role credential access. Need an exact function URL, effective Create/Update URL and permission grants, and code behavior that yields a new IAM capability. Candidate; do not infer full role access from the URL setting.

AddLayerVersionPermission shares a layer version; it does not itself grant the layer publisher or any function execution role. A role pivot would require safely inspecting that exact layer version for usable AWS credentials or proving a downstream function imports controlled code. Neither follows from policy permission. Candidate for content or consumer evidence.

AWS Lambda GetFunction returns function metadata and a time-limited deployment-package download link for ZIP functions; an image function returns an image URI without ECR download access. Package inspection may expose code or embedded secrets but does not grant the function execution role or another principal. The route is documented under post-exploitation. Verified exclusion from principal-to-principal YAML; AWS GetFunction API.

The active aws-lambda-getconfig-secret-identity route covers the exact GetFunctionConfiguration case only when a reviewed usable access key is bound to one named function, one exact IAM user and additional authority. It checks lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration on that resource and rejects a secret reference or arbitrary environment value as proof. The broad old claim is not restored; see src/privilege-escalation-paths/aws/lambda.yaml, peaso/privesc/effective_permissions/aws.py and tests/test_peaso_privesc_v4_exact_user_credentials.py.

GetLayerVersion lets a caller download one layer package, not assume a function role. A principal edge needs safe inspection of that exact package for a usable AWS credential and its added authority; shared code alone is data access. Candidate for credential-content evidence.

The active aws-flink-studio-presigned-url technique already covers this historical duplicate. Evaluator joins one collected RUNNING INTERACTIVE application ARN with its exact ServiceExecutionRole and effective CreateApplicationPresignedUrl permission on the same ARN; execution remains conditional on URL use and notebook behavior. Positive and negative tests in tests/test_peaso_privesc_flink_existing_studio.py cover role and application mismatches, status and denied detail.

CreateTemplateGroupAccessControlEntry grants Enroll or AutoEnroll eligibility to an AD group SID for one template. It does not make the AWS caller an AD group member, issue a certificate, authenticate as an AD user or provide an AWS IAM principal. Verified exclusion from AWS principal-to-principal YAML; AWS AccessControlEntry API and HackTricks Cloud PCA Connector page.

The page describes creating/sending through WorkMail despite SES sandbox limits. That is an email-delivery capability, with no target AWS principal, role assumption, credential grant, or effective IAM permission change. It is a security-control bypass, not an identifiable principal-to-principal route.

The page uses an existing Transfer connector to list, move or delete remote SFTP files. The connector acts with its stored remote credential but the caller does not receive that credential or the connector AWS role. The documented path affects partner files, not another AWS principal's effective permissions.

The page describes deleting or damaging a Verified Permissions store. AWS documents that deletion removes its policies and schema; an application might fail open only if its own error handling is unsafe. No AWS IAM principal gains the store role or another principal's permissions from this operation.

The page changes Secure Browser data-protection redaction patterns. This may expose displayed sensitive data to users of the browser, but the setting names no AWS principal, execution role, or credential that the source obtains.

ApplySecurityGroupsToClientVpnTargetNetwork changes the network identity of a Client VPN association. Even when downstream security groups trust it, the source obtains no AWS IAM role or separate principal permissions; accepted client identity and application access are separate. This is a network authorization finding, not a principal-to-principal edge.

Associating a Client VPN subnet and adding a route can extend network reachability, subject to client authentication, endpoint authorization and downstream controls. These actions do not assign or expose another AWS IAM principal; keep the path in network exposure analysis.

AuthorizeClientVpnIngress broadens which destination network an already authenticated VPN client may reach. It neither creates an AWS IAM principal nor grants the caller a role session; an AWS identity pivot would require a separate service-specific exploit or credential.

GetVpnConnectionDeviceSampleConfiguration can disclose Site-to-Site VPN PSKs for Standard storage. A PSK authenticates a VPN peer, not an AWS IAM principal; tunnel operation additionally needs gateway and routing control. Keep as credential and network exposure, not IAM escalation.

ModifyClientVpnEndpoint can change DNS, routing behavior and connection logging, but it does not grant another AWS principal's IAM actions. Client authentication, endpoint routes and downstream application access remain separate; this is traffic manipulation and telemetry loss.

ModifyVpnConnection and ModifyVpnTunnelOptions can redirect or disable a Site-to-Site VPN peer with the gateway and tunnel prerequisites. They change network connectivity and PSKs, not an AWS role trust or credential. Keep as a network-plane takeover finding.

Timestream UNLOAD executes a SELECT and writes the returned rows plus metadata and manifest to S3. It can expose table data, including a credential only if one was actually stored there, but the UNLOAD permission does not yield an IAM role session or identify a target principal. Keep the data-exposure route in post-exploitation, outside principal-to-principal YAML. AWS UNLOAD concepts and Query API.

Timestream Select authorizes reading named table rows under the caller own identity. Query returns those rows and pagination tokens; no role is assumed and no other AWS principal is identified by the permission. A credential in a particular row would require separate content evidence. Keep as data access outside principal-to-principal YAML. AWS Timestream identity policy examples and Query API.

A misconfigured custom Transfer Family identity provider may log an SFTP/FTP/FTPS password; Logs read permissions can reveal it only when the exact log contains it. The password authenticates a Transfer user, not an IAM or STS principal. File sessions may use a storage role for bounded S3/EFS access but do not yield that role to the log reader. Keep as a credential and file-access risk outside the principal graph; AWS custom IdP docs.

GetDatabase returns the SecretId for a registered SAP HANA ADMIN credential, and GetSecretValue may disclose its database username/password. These authenticate a HANA user, not another AWS IAM principal. Keep the database credential issue outside this principal-to-principal catalog; AWS Systems Manager for SAP GetDatabase and registration docs.

UpdateEnvironment can change a WorkSpaces Thin Client desktopEndpoint, the URL used for a WorkSpaces Applications identity-provider login. Redirecting a desktop login can affect users, but the API does not issue an AWS IAM session or identify a second IAM principal. Any later credential capture or federation pivot needs independent evidence. AWS UpdateEnvironment API reference.

The page associates a VPC with a VPC Lattice service network, creating network reachability while service authentication policies still apply. It does not grant an AWS principal another principal's credentials or IAM permissions; any later service compromise is a separate unproved step.

The page describes changing WAF resource tags. AWS WAF TagResource/UntagResource change tags on the named WAF resource; a separate IAM ABAC policy could change access to that resource, but the operation names no second AWS principal or role-credential path. It cannot establish the required principal-to-principal edge.

GetOidcInfo can disclose the Wickr OIDC client secret and optional IdP-flow tokens. Use still depends on the IdP OAuth flow; no AWS IAM role session or IAM policy grant follows from the read. Retain as integration-secret disclosure (HackTricks Wickr post-exploitation page; AWS GetOidcInfo API).

GetOpentdfConfig can disclose OpenTDF client credentials for a Wickr network. Those authenticate to the OpenTDF integration, not an AWS IAM principal; retain as application/integration-secret disclosure (HackTricks Wickr post-exploitation page; AWS GetOpentdfConfig API).

ListUsers may reveal a pending Wickr invitation enrollment code. That could help claim a Wickr user identity, but no exact IAM role, STS credential or IAM permission grant is identified. Retain as Wickr account takeover risk (HackTricks Wickr post-exploitation page; AWS ListUsers API).

GetRawMessageContent reads a named in-transit message. PutRawMessageContent changes it only from a synchronous Run Lambda rule while the message is eligible. Neither action proves that the message contains a usable AWS credential or reset link, nor identifies the IAM principal it would reach. Without content and credential-subject evidence this is message disclosure or tampering, not an exact principal pivot. AWS WorkMail Message Flow API references.

ModifySamlProperties changes WorkSpaces directory SAML settings, and ModifyCertificateBasedAuthProperties changes desktop certificate authentication. Those operations can affect desktop sign-in, but they do not issue AWS IAM role credentials or identify a second IAM principal. A separate verified desktop credential or federation mapping would be needed for an IAM edge. AWS WorkSpaces API and certificate-based authentication docs.

UpdateWorkspaceImagePermission lets a named account copy a custom WorkSpaces image. Sharing an image does not identify a credential stored inside it, a usable IAM subject or additional AWS authority. An image-content inspection and verified credential-to-principal join would be required; the CSPM does not collect those facts. This is image-sharing exposure, not an exact IAM principal pivot. AWS WorkSpaces image sharing and service authorization docs.

AWS S3 Access Grants GetDataAccess returns a temporary session scoped to the grant's bucket, prefix or object, even though the service assumes the registered location role. The old aws_role edge falsely claimed the role's other permissions. The distinct aws-s3-accessgrants-self-grant route represents only a reviewed, newly effective S3 READ permission for an exact source and prefix. Confirmed against the AWS S3 Access Grants concepts and GetDataAccess API documentation.

The HackTricks S3 Batch Operations page describes CreateJob plus PassRole for bulk copy, ACL, retention or Lambda operations on manifest objects. AWS says Batch Operations assumes the job role to perform the configured object operation; it does not vend its credentials to the caller. The example may expose or alter data at scale, but does not establish that the caller gains another principal identity or new reusable IAM authority. The existing excluded catalog entry is correct for principal-to-principal escalation; AWS Batch Operations permissions and CreateJob docs.

exclusion_technique: Race-replace CloudFormation templates uploaded to a template bucket
review_evidence: PutObject on a CloudFormation template can affect a later deployment only if the exact object is fetched after the write by a known stack operation under a known execution role. Bucket naming and PutBucketNotification alone do not prove that consumer or timing. The current collector lacks object-to-stack/role use and version linkage; candidate pending an exact artifact consumer witness.

exclusion_technique: Replace an S3 object fetched and run by an EC2 managed node
review_evidence: Writing an S3 object gives an EC2 role only if a known instance bootstrap actually fetches and executes that exact object after the write. Native EC2 user data is stored on the instance and does not inherently reference S3. The collector lacks a recorded bootstrap command/object version and its exact instance-profile join; candidate pending those facts. AWS EC2 user data guide.

exclusion_technique: Tamper with a Terraform state file consumed by a pipeline
review_evidence: Changing a Terraform state object affects a later pipeline only if that exact state key is read by a known apply job under a known IAM role and the edited state can cause a privileged action. A .tfstate-looking key and S3 write are insufficient. The collector has no state-backend, pending apply, plan-effect or pipeline-role join; candidate pending those concrete facts.

AWS S3 Files assumes a service role trusting elasticfilesystem.amazonaws.com to synchronize only the selected bucket or prefix. The role and bucket policies must allow those operations; a separate compute client needs a reachable mount target, s3files:ClientMount, source-bucket access and POSIX permissions. CreateFileSystem plus PassRole yields no service-role credentials or general role authority for the caller. The old arbitrary-bucket and bucket-policy-bypass wording has been corrected in HackTricks; AWS S3 Files prerequisites, service authorization and client-access docs.

exclusion_technique: Attach a controlled Studio lifecycle configuration to an existing space
review_evidence: AWS UpdateSpace can attach a lifecycle configuration to an existing space with the matching app type. CSPM now collects ListSpaces/DescribeSpace and joins a shared space to DefaultSpaceSettings.ExecutionRole or a private space to its owner profile role; denied detail remains unresolved. The YAML route is still excluded because it does not yet prove a creatable matching LCC name, effective UpdateSpace authorization on the exact ARN with sagemaker:StudioLifecycleConfigArns context, and a compatible later app start. Do not infer executable role access from the space mapping alone. AWS UpdateSpace, DescribeSpace and SageMaker execution roles/spaces docs.

exclusion_technique: Register an Approved model version in a Model Package Group consumed by auto-deploy automation
review_evidence: AWS says Approved permits deployment but deploys automatically only when a matching EventBridge rule or project workflow exists. Need exact group-level CreateModelPackage right, attacker-controlled readable image or artifact, verified consumer selecting the new Approved version, deployment and target workload role. The collector lists groups and Approved versions but not those consumer or role joins; keep excluded until one exact route can be proven. The HackTricks Cloud page was corrected to state this condition.

exclusion_technique: Replace a mutable ECR image consumed by a later SageMaker Processing job
review_evidence: PutImage on a mutable tag can affect a later Processing job only when the exact future AppSpecification.ImageUri resolves that tag, the image is executable, and the job uses a recorded role with greater authority. Existing processing-job descriptions are historical; they do not prove a pipeline or operator will create another job from the same tag. Candidate for repository/tag, future consumer, execution role and trigger joins.

exclusion_technique: Overwrite S3 code consumed by existing SageMaker training or processing jobs
review_evidence: PutObject can replace an S3 training source bundle or processing input only if the exact configured key is read by a future job and the image actually executes its contents. The current processing projection keeps ImageUri but drops ProcessingInputs; training job facts do not prove a future refresh. Need the exact key, script entrypoint or processing command, trigger, target role and role-readable object. Candidate.

exclusion_technique: Rewrite a notebook-instance lifecycle configuration that runs as the notebook role
review_evidence: Restored as an exact attached notebook lifecycle route. DescribeNotebookInstance supplies the lifecycle configuration name, notebook ARN, status and RoleArn; the evaluator checks service trust and UpdateNotebookInstanceLifecycleConfig on that exact configuration ARN. Next notebook start remains conditional. Focused positive, wrong-configuration, wrong-role, missing-inventory and unsupported-platform tests pass; AWS UpdateNotebookInstanceLifecycleConfig and DescribeNotebookInstance API references.

AWS Scheduler GetSchedule returns a schedule Target including Input and RoleArn. The Input may contain sensitive payload data, but the role ARN is an identifier and the read does not assume it; no specific usable AWS credential or subject is established by the permission. HackTricks Cloud documents this as target-input disclosure. Verified exclusion from principal-to-principal YAML; AWS GetSchedule API.

Reviewed current Snowball post-exploitation section and AWS Snowball S3 export docs. CreateJob with iam:PassRole gives the service a role to copy a selected S3 bucket/key range onto a physical device. The caller receives neither the role credentials nor permission to perform the role's other IAM actions; this is bounded S3 data export, not an exact principal-to-principal edge. Existing exclusion is valid even if an eligible device/job can be ordered.

Reviewed current Snowball post-exploitation section and AWS Snowball job/export docs. UpdateJob changes a New export job's selected S3 data and shipping address while Snowball keeps its stored role; the caller receives no role credentials or general role permissions. This is a bounded physical data-export effect, not an exact principal-to-principal edge. Existing exclusion is valid.

exclusion_technique: Run commands or open sessions on hybrid managed nodes that carry an SSM service role
review_evidence: Restored as aws-ssm-sendcommand-hybrid-role and aws-ssm-startsession-hybrid-role in HackTricks Cloud and synced CSPM. Both evaluators bind the same collected online mi- node, its IamRole to the exact IAM role, platform, managed-instance and shell-document grants; the session variant also requires future OpenDataChannel. Positive and wrong node, role, platform, document, channel, offline and denied-inventory negatives pass in tests/test_peaso_privesc_ssm_hybrid_shell.py. AWS InstanceInformation, SSM agent credential precedence and root-level command docs; runtime credential access remains conditional.

exclusion_technique: Re-point an existing hybrid managed node to a passed role
review_evidence: UpdateManagedInstanceRole plus PassRole can change the role of a named existing hybrid node, but returns no credentials to the caller. A principal pivot requires that the caller also control that node or have a verified shell/command route to it, after the role change, with a valid ssm.amazonaws.com-trusting role. The CSPM collects IamRole and PingStatus but has no exact source foothold-to-node join for this route. AWS UpdateManagedInstanceRole and SSM authorization docs.

exclusion_technique: Set the Default Host Management Configuration role to a passed role
review_evidence: UpdateServiceSetting on the exact DHMC service-setting ARN plus PassRole can choose a regional management role, but it does not give the caller that role. A principal pivot also needs an eligible EC2 host the caller can access or command, working IMDSv2 and agent version, and no instance-profile UpdateInstanceInformation permission that takes precedence. Current collector does not join the DHMC setting to eligible controlled hosts. AWS DHMC guide.

exclusion_technique: Resume another user's disconnected Session Manager session
review_evidence: ResumeSession may reconnect an authorized disconnected shell session, but a port-forward or terminated session does not prove node-role access. Need the exact session ARN, its owner restrictions, state, document and managed-node target, plus that node's IAM role and usable data channel. Current CSPM lacks DescribeSessions state/document/target and the session-to-role join. AWS ResumeSession and SSM authorization docs.

SSM for SAP GetDatabase reveals a database credential SecretId, while Secrets Manager GetSecretValue is separately required to retrieve the password. The recovered user is a SAP HANA database identity, not an AWS IAM role; retain as database credential exposure (AWS Systems Manager for SAP guide).

StartAutomationExecution can run an administrator-authored document under a stored assumeRole, but the caller receives neither its credentials nor all of its permissions. A definite authority edge needs the exact document version, literal role, fixed API steps, allowed parameters and source StartAutomationExecution grant, plus a step whose effect exceeds the source's rights. Current CSPM does not collect full runbook content or parameter constraints. AWS Automation runbook and StartAutomationExecution docs.

exclusion_technique: Open an SSM session into an ECS container with ExecuteCommand enabled
review_evidence: AWS documents that direct ssm:StartSession into an ECS Exec-enabled container is possible outside ecs:ExecuteCommand. A definite role edge needs the exact running task, container runtime target ID, ExecuteCommand agent readiness, task role or EC2 fallback role, allowed shell document, StartSession on the task and OpenDataChannel on the new session. Current collector does not retain the runtime target and session readiness join. AWS ECS Exec guide.

exclusion_technique: Modify a custom SSM document already executed by associations or maintenance windows
review_evidence: UpdateDocument and UpdateDocumentDefaultVersion can plant code in a custom document, but an IAM role edge needs a recorded association or maintenance-window task that uses that document's default version on an exact managed node, with a known role and execution schedule or trigger. The collector records document metadata but not enough consumer-to-document and version semantics. Discovery ListDocuments/GetDocument is optional when the name is known. AWS UpdateDocument and State Manager docs.

exclusion_technique: Attach a customer-managed policy reference to a permission set and re-provision it
review_evidence: AttachCustomerManagedPolicyReferenceToPermissionSet plus ProvisionPermissionSet changes assigned roles only where the named/path-matched customer policy exists. Need exact permission set, assigned account, corresponding policy document and effective added rights, plus a user controlled by the source. Candidate; policy name alone cannot prove admin or source reach (AWS Identity Center permission-set provisioning docs).

exclusion_technique: Attach an AWS-managed policy to a permission set and re-provision it
review_evidence: AttachManagedPolicyToPermissionSet can attach an AWS managed policy such as AdministratorAccess, but an already assigned set needs ProvisionPermissionSet before target roles change. Need exact same set/account, boundary and effective policy evaluation, successful provisioning and source-controlled assigned user/group. Candidate for a direct policy-expansion route (AWS AttachManagedPolicyToPermissionSet and ProvisionPermissionSet APIs).

exclusion_technique: Assign a permission set to a controlled user in an account
review_evidence: CreateAccountAssignment automatically provisions the selected permission set to the target account, but names an Identity Center USER or GROUP, not the caller IAM principal. Need exact controlled subject, usable portal login, target account/permission set, successful async assignment and resulting role. Candidate; the action grant alone is not role reach (AWS CreateAccountAssignment API).

exclusion_technique: Create an admin permission set and assign it to a controlled user in a member account
review_evidence: The self-contained admin set chain needs CreatePermissionSet, AttachManagedPolicyToPermissionSet with AdministratorAccess or PutInlinePolicyToPermissionSet with effective admin, and CreateAccountAssignment for a source-controlled subject. The assignment auto-provisions a new set, but exact instance, target account, local login/subject and successful async status must be joined. Candidate (AWS CreateAccountAssignment and AttachManagedPolicyToPermissionSet APIs).

exclusion_technique: Reset the password of an Identity Center user
review_evidence: UpdatePassword may give the caller a one-time password for a user in the native Identity Center directory, but external-IdP/AD users are managed elsewhere. Need exact native user, password-reset mode, MFA/login usability, assignments and resulting role. Candidate credential-subject route; a generic UpdatePassword grant cannot prove access to an AWS role (HackTricks Identity Center page; AWS directory API docs).

exclusion_technique: Add an inline policy to a permission set and re-provision it
review_evidence: PutInlinePolicyToPermissionSet can replace an inline policy with broader permissions; an assigned set needs ProvisionPermissionSet before its IAM role changes. Need exact set/account, assigned controlled identity, effective policy delta after boundary and SCP, and successful provisioning. Candidate; permission to write the policy by itself does not give the caller that role (AWS ProvisionPermissionSet API).

exclusion_technique: Remove a restricting policy or boundary from a permission set and re-provision it
review_evidence: DeletePermissionsBoundaryFromPermissionSet removes one set-level boundary; it adds no rights if the remaining policies grant nothing beyond the old boundary. Need exact set/account, existing restrictive boundary, effective before/after policy delta, ProvisionPermissionSet and a source-controlled assigned subject. Candidate (AWS DeletePermissionsBoundaryFromPermissionSet and ProvisionPermissionSet APIs).

AWS GetActivityTask can supply a live token and input for an exact Activity, while SendTaskSuccess can return attacker-selected JSON to that paused execution. A role-mediated AWS principal edge exists only if the collected state-machine definition and current execution join this callback output to a downstream sensitive AWS action under a named execution role, with attacker-controlled parameter paths and effective target permissions. A fixed Choice/Lambda/business-action branch may be serious without giving the caller the execution role or general IAM authority. CSPM does not collect a live token or prove the ASL dataflow/sink join; retain as candidate, never infer a full role edge from callback actions alone. AWS GetActivityTask, SendTaskSuccess and Step Functions callback integration docs.

exclusion_technique: Modify the definition of an existing state machine keeping its role
review_evidence: DescribeStateMachine collection retains exact stateMachineArn, roleArn, status and type; the active PassRole route checks update and start on the same active machine. HackTricks says a definition-only update can use the stored role without PassRole, and AWS UpdateStateMachine makes roleArn optional, but the AWS Service Authorization Reference lists iam:PassRole as a dependent action for UpdateStateMachine. The no-PassRole variant needs a verified authorization witness before restoration; the API schema alone does not settle the conflict.

exclusion_technique: Obtain a privileged root-user session in a member account with sts:AssumeRoot
review_evidence: AssumeRoot can issue member-account root credentials only from the Organizations management or IAM delegated-admin account after centralized root sessions are enabled. Every request requires one of five task policies and the session lasts at most 15 minutes; an aws_account_admin edge would overstate it. Candidate bounded root-task permission route needs organization/member/delegation and feature-state joins plus task-policy-specific target authority (AWS AssumeRoot API).

exclusion_technique: Assign Supply Chain application administrator to a controlled Identity Center user
review_evidence: The page and AWS Supply Chain authorization reference bind AssignAdminPermissionsToUser to one application instance and federated user. It creates an application administrator, not an IAM role session, Identity Center permission set, or new IAM policy. Track this as service-plane access; the documented operation cannot identify a second AWS IAM principal's permissions.

exclusion_technique: Dry-run replacement canary code under the canary's execution role
review_evidence: AWS StartCanaryDryRun accepts replacement Code and an optional ExecutionRoleArn for an existing canary. The collector declares synthetics:DescribeCanaries and the evaluator binds a named collected canary to its recorded role. A valid route also needs a compatible existing runtime (Puppeteer 10+, Playwright 2+, Python Selenium 5.1+ or Node.js 3.0+), no conflicting in-progress dry run, the exact generated Lambda function and code-layer authorization, and the exact requested role if ExecutionRoleArn is supplied. A successful code-bearing execution is not proved by an HTTP 200 response. Keep the candidate excluded until those joins are implemented; the protected collector source-admission epoch also remains to be reconciled. AWS StartCanaryDryRun, safe-canary-update, Canary, and service authorization docs.

DescribeConnector identifies a Secrets Manager secret for remote SFTP authentication; GetSecretValue is separately required. Those credentials authenticate to the remote SFTP server, not another AWS IAM principal. Retain as bounded external-service credential exposure (AWS Transfer SFTP connector guide).

UpdateServer or API Gateway response edits select a bounded Transfer file-session role, not general IAM authority. The Lambda UpdateFunctionCode variant can additionally run attacker code under the configured IdP Lambda execution role when Transfer invokes it; the generic Lambda route currently requires direct InvokeFunction and the collector omits IdentityProviderDetails.Function. Need exact server-to-function/role join, active SFTP login trigger and code-signing checks before claiming that IAM role edge. AWS Transfer custom-IdP and Lambda code-signing docs.

ImportSshPublicKey adds a key to a service-managed SFTP user. It can grant bounded S3/EFS file operations through that user, subject to home and session policy, but does not give the source an IAM role session or AWS API credentials. AWS Transfer service-managed user and session-policy guides.

CreateUser/UpdateUser/CreateAccess/UpdateAccess can bind a Transfer-trusting role to an SFTP or directory identity. Authentication uses that role only for Transfer S3/EFS file operations and never gives the caller the role session or unrelated AWS API authority. AWS Transfer user-role and session-policy guides.

Changing the legacy custom-IdP secret may alter a Transfer login and its file-session role, but the returned role is used by Transfer for bounded S3/EFS access. The secret write does not expose or grant the role credentials. AWS Transfer custom-IdP and user-role guides.

A managed Transfer workflow uses the passed role for fixed storage steps or to invoke a separately configured Lambda on an upload. Creating or attaching the workflow does not give its caller that role session or arbitrary API execution. AWS Transfer workflow-execution-role and custom-step guides.

Replacing an AS2 partner signing certificate may cause Transfer to accept partner messages, an application identity and data-integrity issue. It does not grant another AWS IAM principal or its permissions. AWS Transfer AS2 monitoring guide.

Duplicate of aws-pa-persist-s01-01. Creating or using an ACME external account binding can let a registered ACME client request or revoke certificates within the associated role ACM permissions. It does not provide the IAM role session or general AWS API authority to the caller. Verified exclusion from AWS principal-to-principal YAML; AWS External account bindings and CreateAcmeExternalAccountBinding API.

UpdateApplication can repoint a Connect agent workspace application and expose contact data to an attacker origin. The page does not identify any AWS IAM principal or credential acquired by the source; agent browser access alone is not a principal-to-principal route.

UpdateBrowserSettings can install an extension in future Secure Browser sessions. It does not name an exact AWS principal or credential; any later captured credential requires its own observed identity and is not proven by the policy change.

A rogue SAML or OIDC provider can create an independent login path to a WorkSpaces Secure Browser portal. Portal login is not an AWS IAM session and the page does not name an exact AWS principal gained by the source.

AWS confirms primary and secondary Cognito replicas keep separate password-failure counters, so a public client can make more independent guesses. The route has no IAM principal action and does not identify a valid user password, a successful challenge, an MFA result or credentials for an exact other principal. This is an authentication attack possibility, not a principal-to-principal edge that a read-only CSPM inventory can determine. The existing excluded catalog entry remains correct; AWS Cognito multi-Region replication and authentication docs.

AgentCore Runtime credentials are inside its microVM, and AWS now requires MMDSv2 for new invocations. A GET-only SSRF is insufficient; a token-capable SSRF or usable legacy session is application/runtime evidence, not an IAM action or configuration fact that identifies an exact role session. No such exploit or credential response is collected, so the existing excluded entry is correct for the principal graph; AWS AgentCore Runtime security and troubleshooting docs.

An ECS-on-EC2 task may reach the host IMDS role only when the source controls code in that exact task and metadata routing, network mode and host firewall permit it. The current AWS principal graph does not prove a task code foothold or IMDS reachability from it. Candidate for exact task-to-host and network proof, not an IAM grant alone.

A source with root or container-runtime control of a connected ECS host can read co-located task credentials, but host control and actual task placement are runtime facts. ECS inventory records task and container-instance IDs but not source ownership of the host socket or credential endpoint access. Candidate for exact same-host foothold and role join.

AWS Lambda supplies execution-role credentials to running code through environment variables. Merely having InvokeFunction or reading function configuration does not expose that process environment. The route requires code execution or a vulnerable handler, an observed credential response and exact target role; none follows from cloud IAM permissions or read-only function metadata. Keep the host/runtime credential-theft possibility out of the principal graph; AWS Lambda environment-variable guide.

The Strategy Recommendations collector may hold AWS credential material on its host, but this route starts with local root, Docker or filesystem access to that host and a usable secret tuple. AWS account inventory cannot establish that foothold, the secret value or its exact IAM owner. The existing excluded entry correctly avoids inventing a principal edge from Migration Hub configuration; AWS collector setup and prerequisites docs.

An SNS/SQS/Kinesis/DynamoDB/Logs/metric producer can cause an already configured Lambda consumer to run, but this alone does not yield its role. Need exact enabled source-to-function path and role, plus handler evidence that a caller-controlled field drives a specific privileged AWS action and useful result. CSPM lacks handler input-to-action semantics; permission-only graph edges would be false positives. AWS Lambda event-source docs.

AWS IoT can invoke an existing Lambda with MQTT message data, but exact writable topic, enabled matching SQL rule, Lambda action and function invoke policy must join. A role edge additionally needs handler logic that turns the payload into a privileged AWS action under the function's recorded role. CSPM lacks that semantic proof; iot:Publish alone is insufficient. AWS IoT Lambda rule-action docs.

Lex V2 invokes a configured fulfillment Lambda only for the matching intent and enabled hook after required slots are filled. A runtime request can trigger application-specific behavior, but does not give the caller the Lambda execution-role session. The route identifies no handler operation, returned AWS credential or second IAM principal. It is bounded application behavior, not a principal-to-principal privilege escalation. AWS Lex fulfillment and Lambda hook guides.

WAF records can expose request fields, but an application cookie or bearer token authenticates to the application, not automatically to an AWS IAM principal. This route does not contain a complete verified AWS credential or exact IAM subject; WAF log and sample availability alone cannot establish one. It duplicates the bounded WAF request-reading route and is not an identifiable principal pivot. AWS WAF logging and sampled-request docs.

GetRemoteAccessSession may return interactive and Appium endpoints for one live test device, enabling control of its app session. AWS describes these as device-control URLs, not IAM or STS credentials; no execution role is returned to the caller. Any AWS credential later found in the app would require separate content and subject proof. Keep as application-session takeover outside the principal graph; AWS Device Farm endpoint docs.

CreateStreamSessionConnection can reconnect to an ACTIVE or PENDING_CLIENT_RECONNECTION stream while preserving in-app state. AWS documents the reconnect as WebRTC application access, not issuance of the stream's execution-role credentials. It can expose app data or a private network, but no second AWS principal is reached by this API alone; AWS GameLift Streams session docs.
Duplicate of aws-v3-05. Attacker IdP can authenticate a WorkSpaces Secure Browser user, but portal login is not an IAM role session and the route names no exact AWS principal gained.

The SiteWise page and AWS CreateAccessPolicy API support grants to a Monitor portal IAM user or Identity Center user, subject to legacy account availability. The active aws-sitewise-createaccesspolicy-portal-self-grant models only an exact reviewed self-user permission differential. A different controlled identity still needs a typed source-control and effective-access join; the page IAM-role example was corrected because the API description does not list roles as supported portal identities.

CreateChatToken can issue a WebSocket room token with an application-provided userId and selected chat capabilities. That token may impersonate an application user for room messages or moderation, but neither userId nor token is an IAM/STS principal credential. Keep this chat risk outside the AWS principal graph; AWS CreateChatToken API.

BatchCreateDelegationByAssessment can give a named role control-set review authority. Exact source-to-role edge needs source control or assumability of that role, effective permission on both assessment and control set, and resulting delegation; the API does not grant sts:AssumeRole.

GetWirelessDevice can return LoRaWAN/Sidewalk keys useful for device cloning or wireless traffic manipulation, but these authenticate a wireless device rather than an IAM user or role. No second AWS principal or API authority is granted by those keys. Keep as a device-identity risk outside the principal graph; AWS IoT Wireless device and LoRaWAN docs.

A redirected connector may disclose an ERP or database credential read by its instance role, conditional on endpoint acceptance and actual authentication. That downstream credential is not an AWS IAM principal credential; no exact source-to-IAM-role edge is shown.

The ProcurementPortalSharedSecret belongs to an external procurement integration, not an AWS IAM or STS principal. Reading it or changing the preference may expose or redirect invoice data, but does not give the source another AWS principal. AWS verification and connection testing are separate steps; keep this business-impact route out of the principal escalation graph.

DescribeUserPoolClient may return a Cognito confidential app secret usable for configured OAuth flows. It is not an IAM credential. An identity-pool mapping to an exact AWS role would require separate evidence absent from this route.

GetAccessor can return a BILLING_TOKEN for Ethereum/Polygon JSON-RPC usage billed to the victim, but that bearer is a Managed Blockchain service credential, not an IAM/STS session or another principal. It does not disclose wallet private keys. Keep paid-node misuse outside the principal graph; AWS accessor token docs.

GetIceServerConfig returns temporary TURN relay credentials; signed signaling still requires the source's ConnectAsViewer or ConnectAsMaster permission on the channel. TURN credentials authenticate to the media relay, not IAM/STS. Peer impersonation or media exposure is an application-plane risk, not another AWS principal; AWS GetIceServerConfig and ConnectAsViewer docs.

StartExecution can only reach a Lambda execution role through a specific state-machine input mapping and proven dangerous Lambda handler behavior. Require exact machine, task target, reviewed handler code, effective start permission and role; invocation alone is insufficient.

A caller-controlled HTTP Task endpoint can receive EventBridge Connection credentials if the workflow and role allow it. Those are remote-service credentials, not the state-machine execution role or an exact IAM principal gained by the source.

A live callback ID and permission on its owning execution can submit a result, but an AWS role edge needs reviewed durable-function logic showing that this exact result reaches a privileged AWS action under its execution role. The callback action neither discovers IDs nor proves that branch.

AWS CLI stores Identity Center access tokens in a local user cache. Reusing another user's token requires access to that user's device/files, a still-valid token and an assigned account role; none is an IAM permission or fact recorded by the AWS collector. The cache path alone identifies neither a reachable victim nor a usable role session. This remains endpoint credential theft, not a determinable cloud principal edge; AWS CLI IAM Identity Center tutorial.

AWS CLI caches assumed-role temporary credentials locally and stores configured user keys in the user credential file. Reuse requires another user's file access, unexpired usable material and the exact credential subject, none of which an AWS account inventory or IAM grant establishes. The excluded catalog entry correctly keeps host-local credential theft out of a cloud principal graph; AWS CLI role and configuration guides.

The HackTricks page describes a local AWS VPN Client credential file and a possible temporary metrics-role credential. The path needs another user's local file access, valid secret/session material and an exact target role; it supplies no AWS API permission that gives those facts. The CSPM does not inspect endpoint files, so a cloud IAM graph would invent the credential edge. The existing excluded catalog entry remains correct.

TagResources requires both generic and native tagging authorization. Exact ABAC route needs the mutable resource, chosen tag value, both effective permissions, a specific policy condition granting a new AWS action, and deny analysis. Tag permission alone is not escalation.

The described route starts from a compromised integration endpoint and depends on its application responses, whether the agent forwards credentials or performs a privileged tool action, and the exact role involved. Endpoint inventory or a named agent role proves none of those steps. No fixed AWS IAM action or collected execution evidence yields a determinate principal-to-principal path, so the existing excluded catalog entry is appropriate.
CreateAppInstanceUser/Admin promotes a Chime messaging user or bot, not an AWS IAM principal. Chime still requires the calling AWS session to have IAM authorization for each messaging action.

DetachPolicy, UpdatePolicy, DisablePolicyType or MoveAccount from a management/delegated principal can remove a restrictive SCP on an exact member account, but SCPs never grant IAM permission. A principal-to-principal edge requires a separately identified controlled member-account IAM user/role, effective action previously denied solely by that SCP, exact organization hierarchy/attachments and source mutation authority; no escalation for management-account principals (AWS SCP guide).

organizations:PutResourcePolicy from the management account can delegate selected Organizations policy-management actions to a member-account principal. The recipient must also have matching identity-based IAM permissions, and only supported delegated actions/resources are possible. Require exact accepted policy/principal/action/resource, source permission and recipient IAM/guardrail authorization; PutResourcePolicy alone is not usable authority (AWS Organizations delegation guide).

CreateUser plus BatchAssociateUserStack grants a service portal foothold. An AWS role edge additionally needs completed mailbox/password flow, usable stack, command execution in an app or desktop, and a fleet IAM machine role whose credentials the session can access.

CreateAccessGrant can give a named IAM user or role SPACE_ADMIN authority in one Omni space. Exact source-to-principal route needs proven source control of that principal plus authentication, effective IAM/space authorization and operator-role limits; the grant neither mints IAM credentials nor makes a role assumable.

ElastiCache ModifyUser changes an existing Valkey/Redis user password, authentication mode or access string. It can increase cache data-plane access if the user is attached and reachable, including when IAM authentication is configured, but it does not vend or assume an AWS IAM role. A secret stored in a particular cache key would require separate observed content and credential-to-principal evidence. Verified exclusion from AWS principal-to-principal YAML; AWS ModifyUser API and ElastiCache RBAC guide.

ElastiCache CreateUser and user-group changes can add a cache RBAC identity to a replication group. Its access string controls cache keys and commands, not AWS IAM actions or another principal session. A later credential read from cache contents is not established by these API permissions. Verified exclusion from AWS principal-to-principal YAML; AWS ElastiCache RBAC guide.

MemoryDB CreateUser and UpdateACL can place a new cache user in an ACL attached to a cluster. AWS documents that the ACL determines engine-user access; it does not create or assume an IAM role. A later credential read from an actual cache key would need separate content and subject evidence. Verified exclusion from AWS principal-to-principal YAML; AWS UpdateACL and User APIs.

MemoryDB UpdateUser can change the password or access string of a cache user already attached through an ACL. That is control of an engine identity subject to cluster reachability, not a new AWS IAM principal or role session. Potential secrets in cache rows require separate observation. Verified exclusion from AWS principal-to-principal YAML; AWS MemoryDB UpdateUser and User APIs.

Duplicate of aws-v3-36 service identity risk. Chime AppInstance admin status persists for a controlled messaging user/bot but grants no AWS IAM permissions; later calls still require the caller own authorized AWS session.

The active catalog covers the narrower Studio user-profile lifecycle route as aws-sagemaker-attach-studio-lifecycle-config-user-profile. Domain default needs exact affected profile or space, controlled compatible configuration, effective UpdateDomain permission and later app start before naming an execution role.

CreateUser can make a Connect-managed Admin service login when the instance and profile ARNs are authorized. It does not create IAM credentials or give the caller a second AWS principal. SAML mode needs separate federation proof.
UpdateNamespace sets a Redshift database administrator password. That SQL identity is not an IAM principal and the route reveals no second AWS principal credential.

UpdateFHIRDatastore can replace a SMART token-validation Lambda that returns a role ARN for HealthLake FHIR requests. Exact bounded role-backed route needs the datastore, controlled validator, valid token, Lambda invoke policy, trusted service role and allowed FHIR actions; no general role credentials are issued.
UpdateAutonomousDatabase can reset Oracle ADMIN password. That is a database login, not AWS IAM or OCI tenancy authority, and the page identifies no second AWS principal.

AssociateAdminAccount sets the default FMS administrator account with full organizational policy scope; PutAdminAccount is a distinct route for additional or updated administrator accounts with optional limited scope, after onboarding. Both designate accounts rather than grant an IAM principal rights by themselves. Exact source-to-principal route needs effective management-account API permission, eligible member and organization state, a controlled IAM identity in the member, its FMS permissions and actual scope. AWS FMS AssociateAdminAccount and PutAdminAccount APIs.

PutAdminAccount designates an organization member account. Exact route needs proven controlled identity there, effective Network Security Manager actions, all-features/trusted-access prerequisites and matching scope; account designation alone does not identify a second principal.
GetDbInstance and GetSecretValue can expose InfluxDB engine credentials and permit planting a native API token. These are database identities, not AWS IAM credentials or another AWS principal.

The Lightsail API returns a database master password, not IAM credentials. Instance SSH keys could lead to host access, but the page does not establish an instance role, metadata credential or exact AWS principal transition.

UpdateDomainConfig can grant ESHttp resource-policy access to a named IAM principal. Exact route needs source control of that identity, effective update permission, completed policy, reachable endpoint and fine-grained-access/deny limits; it is not role assumption.

PutResourcePolicy can allow a controlled external IAM principal to describe or change a named seller entity. Exact route requires source control of that principal and its own applicable IAM authorization; the policy is entity-scoped, not seller-account access.
AssumeImpersonationRole yields a WorkMail EWS bearer token scoped by mailbox rules. It is not sts:AssumeRole and the token cannot call AWS APIs as another IAM principal.

A member account leaving its organization loses its inherited SCP/RCP guardrails, but the caller must be allowed organizations:LeaveOrganization and the account must meet standalone-account prerequisites. The target IAM principal must already have identity/resource authorization blocked by the removed guardrail; no new privilege follows from leaving alone, and organization-path trusts may also cease to work (AWS Organizations/SCP guides).

GetId and GetCredentialsForIdentity can give a public guest a session for the pool's unauthenticated role, but this enhanced-flow session is intersected with Cognito's inline and managed scope-down policies. The AWS-managed policy grants no IAM or STS action, so the session cannot exercise the role's unrestricted authority or directly pivot to another IAM principal. The starting client is anonymous rather than an existing IAM principal.
