This is a bounded public-access exposure; the distinct Basic-flow full-role route is also outside the IAM-principal-to-IAM-principal map, although it can be a serious public identity-pool exposure. AWS Cognito IAM roles and AmazonCognitoUnAuthedIdentitiesSessionPolicy docs.

The basic Cognito identity-pool flow is a real public-client route to an IAM role when an eligible user has a usable identity-pool token, classic flow is enabled, role mappings do not block Basic flow, and the role trusts that pool and authentication method. GetId and GetOpenIdToken do not require an existing AWS IAM source principal, so this cannot be an IAM-principal-to-IAM-principal edge. The IAM-authorized developer-token classic route remains cataloged separately. Report public classic-flow role exposure in identity-pool security checks rather than assigning it to every AWS principal. AWS Cognito authentication flow and GetId API.

Cognito SignUp is a public app-client operation for which AWS does not evaluate IAM policies. A self-registered user normally must confirm and authenticate before receiving a user-pool token, and an IAM role additionally needs a linked identity pool and matching trust. This starts from a public customer identity, not an existing AWS IAM principal; SignUp alone identifies no second IAM principal reached by a scanned IAM source. Review the public sign-up and identity-pool role exposure as configuration risks outside the principal-to-principal map. AWS SignUp API and self-registration guide.

The page's public web client obtains Cognito guest credentials to call Lex runtime APIs. This is the same enhanced-flow guest session as aws-v3-59, limited by the role and Cognito's scope-down policies; Lex invocation, session access or fulfillment effects do not grant another IAM principal. The starting client is anonymous rather than an existing IAM principal. Review broad Lex grants as public service exposure, not as a full-role privilege-escalation edge. AWS Cognito IAM roles and Lex V2 IAM permission docs.

DisableOperatorApp plus EnableOperatorApp can install attacker IdP and pass exact operator role. Exact bounded role route needs both permissions, PassRole, compatible trust, accepted attacker authentication and named operator actions reachable through that role; no raw STS credential is returned.

Deleting or detaching a policy can remove an explicit Deny only when the source is authorized to mutate that exact policy/attachment despite all other denies and boundaries. A verified escalation requires the same controlled target principal, exact statement/attachment, previously blocked action and effective permission after removal; deleting an unrelated policy or a permissions boundary does not establish the delta (AWS IAM policy evaluation and deletion APIs).
EVS-managed vCenter, NSX, SDDC Manager and ESX secrets contain VMware administrator credentials, not IAM principal credentials; reading them gives no exact second AWS principal.
EVS connector secret holds VCF appliance credentials. This authenticates to VMware, not AWS IAM, and does not identify another AWS principal.

Distinct from aws-v3-51: AssociateAdminAccount sets the default administrator with full scope, while PutAdminAccount can create or update an additional administrator with optional limited scope and requires prior onboarding. DisassociateAdminAccount removes rather than grants a designation. The exact account-to-controlled-IAM-identity join and effective FMS rights remain uncollected, so no principal edge is asserted. AWS FMS AssociateAdminAccount and PutAdminAccount APIs.
ModifyReplicationGroup may add an attacker-known legacy Valkey/Redis AUTH token. It gives cache data-plane access, not another AWS IAM principal.

EnableDelegatedAdminAccount designates a member account, not an IAM principal. Exact source-to-identity edge requires management-account permission, organization all-features/incumbent-admin handling and a controlled identity in the selected account with effective Inspector actions.
ResetPassword yields WorkMail mailbox credentials, which are application login credentials and cannot call AWS APIs as another IAM user or role.
Policy-store alias rebind changes application Cedar decisions, not IAM identity policy or role credentials. It does not transfer source to another AWS principal.
Identity-source change may trust attacker-issued application JWTs, but Verified Permissions still requires a separately authorized SigV4 caller and does not grant AWS IAM role authority.
Cedar policy can give application admin authority but does not alter IAM policies or create AWS credentials; decision APIs do not execute application actions.

GetSampledRequests returns a sample of web requests, potentially with headers; request sampling and log redaction are separate settings. A recovered application session can affect the application, but does not itself become another IAM principal. No sampled request content, complete AWS credential, verified subject or added authority is collected by CSPM. Treat as sensitive request-data exposure, not an IAM role edge. AWS WAF sampled-request and logging docs.
